id: Comfy Concert for AS+ - The Chamber Pot Pourri Ensemble, presenting the Amada Quartet-13 Maida Vale Road, Roseneath, Wellington 6011, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: Comfy Concert for AS+ - The Chamber Pot Pourri Ensemble, presenting the Amada Quartet
venue: 13 Maida Vale Road, Roseneath, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
🎵 Join us for an afternoon of beautiful music and community spirit! 🎵


Enjoy Beautiful Chamber Music with a View! Relax with a cuppa and a biscuit (koha appreciated!) while listening to expertly curated chamber music at an intimate venue in one of Wellington’s most stunning locations.

Helene Pohl (violin) and Rolf Gjelsten (cello), as the Chamber Pot Pourri Ensemble, are getting together with friends to play a series of intimate concerts that support some of their favourite causes – Arohanui Strings+ included (www.arohanuistrings.org).

The Amada Quartet - Violinists Lorna Zhang and Esther Oh, violist Juliet Park and cellist Esther Lee - is a collaboration between students and recent graduates of the Auckland University School of Music, and the New Zealand School of Music (Te Kōkī) Victoria University of Wellington.

Lorna and the two Esthers hail from Auckland, and Juliet is from Christchurch. Together they perform through the Auckland Philharmonia Aspiring Musicians Programme, and have received mentorship from icons of the New Zealand chamber music scene, such as Monique Lapins, Ashley Brown, Helene Pohl and Rolf Gjelsten.  

Prior to the concert they are spending a week in Wellington receiving intensive coaching from Helene and Rolf.

The Amada Quartet have also performed in a a master class for members of the Takacs Quartet. It's going to be such a great afternoon!

This Comfy Concert programme includes:

Beethoven – Quartet no. 1 in F Major, opus 18#1

Lorna Zhang – new work

Mendelssohn – Quartet in f minor, opus 80

Schubert – Allegro from Quintet in C Major with Rolf Gjelsten

🎻 (programmes and artists may change - but hopefully not!)

Location

The Long Hall overlooks Point Jerningham with views of Te Whanganui-a-Tara/Wellington Harbour. See the Google map location. You can park on Maida Vale Rd or on Roseneath School tennis court and follow the signs. Or on foot or bike, use the footpath up from Carlton Gore Road or from Maida Vale Road near Roseneath School.

BYO cushion and slippers (it is a shoes-off venue) is advised.




Rolf Gjelsten (cello), Helene Pohl (violin)

long_description:
Calling all music lovers!

Sound Stage is a monthly evening of live acoustic music, bringing together performers and audiences.

Each month features one main act, giving local and amateur musicians a stage to shine while guests enjoy great live music in the Hutt Valley.

Feel like moving? There’s space to dance, or simply relax and soak up the acoustic vibes.

Want a bite to eat while you enjoy the music? Order from our menu — grazing plates, snacks, and meals are available to keep the night going.

Perfect for a midweek night out with friends, fellow music enthusiasts, or anyone looking for an affordable evening of acoustic music, dancing, and good food.

Carylann with Steve Poulton

Bringing together powerful vocals, outstanding musicianship, and a passion for country music, this dynamic duo delivers a high-energy show packed with country favourites, original songs, and plenty of entertainment. A night guaranteed to have you singing along and smiling from ear to ear!

Award-winning singer-songwriter Carylann joins forces with acclaimed guitarist and vocalist Steve Poulton for an unforgettable evening of country music. Expect powerful vocals, exceptional musicianship, and a foot-stompin' mix of country classics and original favourites.

venue: 167 Riddiford Street, Newtown, Wellington 6021, New Zealand
long_description:
For our fourth all-night-long session, Yendor!

A close collaborator with DT, he has been perfecting his craft as a DJ and producer since the last decade, waiting in the smoke and shadows for when he is needed most. A dance-floor vigilante; Yendor’s time has come. Driven by a taste for serious tension and release, we hope you are prepared for what's in store.

Don't worry, we'd never do this without the hi-fi Torque rig, the Torqmobile, providing us with all our premium bass and treble needs.

With releases on European labels 39 Records and Halbtrocken Exclusive, Yendor recently kicked off the DT label with his 'Fort Ballance' EP. No doubt you will hear some of it on the night. His armoury holds powerful weapons, many of which are set to be utilised.

See you at Moon Bar, on August 21st, for Session 13 of Dance Therapy.

id: Jazz and Beyond Workshops 2026-91 Kelburn Parade, Kelburn, Wellington 6012, New Zealand  ·  Accessibility info-Humanitix
name: Jazz and Beyond Workshops 2026
venue: 91 Kelburn Parade, Kelburn, Wellington 6012, New Zealand  ·  Accessibility info
long_description:
Jazz and Beyond for students 19 and under

December 14–17, 2026

Coordinated by Chris Beernink, Dave Wilson, Daniel Hayles, Andrew, Faleatua, Lance Philip. Proudly supported by the Tauranga Jazz Society.

Take your playing to the next level at the Jazz and Beyond Workshops! Young musicians from across Aotearoa come together to dive into jazz and connected styles, working closely with some of the country’s leading performers and educators. In a friendly, inclusive environment, you’ll grow your skills, make new musical connections, and learn alongside other students your age from all around the motu.

Here’s what’s in store:

small group ensembles led by professional musicians

developing improvisation skills in supportive settings

an introduction to music production

listening sessions that expand your skills

inclusive jam sessions where all are welcome

ensemble performances at the end of week concert

And more!

If you're 19 or under with at least a year of experience on your instrument or in vocal training, you’re welcome to join. Choose from trumpet, trombone, saxophone, clarinet, flute, bass, piano, guitar, drums, vibraphone, or voice.

The workshops are held at the New Zealand School of Music-Te Kōkī at Te Herenga Waka-Victoria University of Wellington. Follow the Jazz and Beyond Workshops on Instagram or Facebook for the latest updates. Email jazzandbeyondworkshops@gmail.com with any questions.

Schedule

The workshops run 9:00am-4:30pm Monday through Thursday, with evening activities including concerts and our inclusive jam sessions Monday, Tuesday, and Wednesday. Students perform in a closing concert on Thursday afternoon.

Accommodation

Students arrange their own accommodation. Often students from outside Wellington stay together in groups with a parent chaperone. Options for housing near Victoria University of Wellington include backpacker hostels and hotels. If you have a group of 15 or more, University Student Housing can been booked at Cumberland House. Contact info for this option is via email at Cumberland-House@vuw.ac.nz or by phone at +64 4 463 4770.

Meals

Lunch for the four days is available for purchase at many convenient locations on campus, or students may bring their own lunch.

Equipment

Provided equipment includes drum kits, guitar and bass amps, pianos/keyboards, microphones and PAs for vocalists.

All brass and wind players should bring their own instruments.

Drummers: you are required to bring your own cymbals, sticks, and hi-hat clutch.

Guitarists and bass players: you are required to bring your own instruments as well as cables (leads).

Preparation

All students with one year of experience on an instrument or in vocal training have the skills required to participate, so no musical preparation is required. On the first day, students will play a very short audition to be placed in an appropriate ensemble. Guidelines for this short audition will be sent to all registered participants in advance of the workshops.

Cost

Early bird price: $325 - register by 19th October

Standard price $350 - after 19th October

Registration is open to all until all spots are filled.

We are dedicated to ensuring all students can participate in the workshops without financial constraints. If the cost poses a barrier, please email us at jazzandbeyondworkshops@gmail.com and we will find a solution to facilitate your participation!

id: Deep Listening Sound Bath at Erskine Chapel-31 Avon Street, Island Bay, Wellington 6023, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: Deep Listening Sound Bath at Erskine Chapel
venue: 31 Avon Street, Island Bay, Wellington 6023, New Zealand
long_description:
A Deep Listening Sound Bath inside the sublime acoustics of Erskine Chapel

Limited door sales for $50

Please bring a yoga mat, pillow, eye mask and blanket - or whatever it is you need to feel most warm and comfortable. Dress comfortably.

Discover the transformative effects of sound therapy with this 1.5hr-hour sound bath experience.

During this session, participants will be surrounded by the resonant vibrations of strings and gongs carefully designed to induce deep states of relaxation and calm. As you settle into the experience, allow the soothing tones to wash over you, releasing tension and promoting a sense of inner peace.

Scientific studies have highlighted the benefits of sound therapy in reducing stress and promoting overall well-being. The rhythmic patterns and overtones of the gongs and other instruments can help entrain brainwaves, leading to a meditative state and improved mental clarity.

Beyond the immediate effects, many participants report experiencing lasting benefits such as improved sleep, reduced anxiety, and enhanced mood following a gong bath session. By immersing yourself in the healing vibrations of the sounds, you can tap into a deeper sense of relaxation and rejuvenation.

Whether you're looking to unwind after a long day or explore new avenues of self-care, this 1.5hr-hour sound bath offers a unique opportunity to reconnect with yourself and find balance amidst the hustle and bustle of daily life. There will be cups of tea available afterwards to help us integrate and ground.

*THIS EVENT IS RESTRICTED TO 40 PEOPLE ONLY**

Disclaimer
Sound baths are safe and supportive for most people. However, please consult your doctor or mental health professional before attending if you:-have a pacemaker or other implanted medical device
-live with epilepsy or a sound-sensitive condition
-are in the first trimester of pregnancy
-are experiencing severe or unmanaged mental health challenges (such as psychosis, schizophrenia, or PTSD)If you have recent injuries, surgeries, or other health concerns, let me know so we can make sure you’re comfortable.

Everyone responds differently to sound. If at any point during the session you feel overwhelmed or uncomfortable, you are welcome to sit up, move gently, or step outside. Your wellbeing always comes first

About Us

Rebecca Struthers is a violinist with the New Zealand Symphony Orchestra, and has spent many years discovering the connection in small ensemble playing. Following a lifelong interest in healing modalities, she is currently completing her training in the therapeutic use of music in medical settings. For this collaboration, Rebecca brings the deep earthy voice of bass violin into the soundscape, to collectively explore resonance, vibration and stillness.

Isaac Smith is a New Zealand double bass player, multi-instrumentalist, and electronic musician based in Wellington (Te Whanganui-a-Tara). He is a prominent figure in Aotearoa's experimental, free-improvisation, and underground music scenes, frequently performing at Wellington's Pyramid Club.


Erika Grant is a musician and astrologer based in Te Whanganui-a-Tara. She has many years of musical experience, in all sorts of forms. Erika has an interest in the healing properties of sound for mental and physical wellbeing, which she currently explores through her gong bathing practice.

name: Daniel Champagne LIVE at Old St Paul's | Wellington (a Family Friendly Concert)
venue: 34 Mulgrave Street, Pipitea, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
The young virtuoso, recently described as “the finest guitar player of this generation,” has fallen in love with New Zealand! — and after sold-out shows around the globe, he’ll bring his now-famous live show to 25 intimate venues across the country in 2026!

“Do whatever it takes to get in the front row!”
– Roots Magazine, UK

“A generational talent that must be seen to be believed.”
– The Calgary Herald, CANADA

OLD ST PAUL'S - WELLINGTON

✨ August 12, 2026

✨ 7:00pm doors / 7:30pm show

✨ Seated Concert

✨ FAMILY FRIENDLY with cheaper $20 tickets for under 18s

Don’t miss your chance to experience live music at its finest!

WHAT THE PRESS SAY

“The word ‘prodigy’ seems to entirely fall short of this soft-spoken young man’s skills. He coaxes sounds and melodies out of his instrument that literally drop jaws.”
– The Calgary Herald, Canada

“Today I saw the future of folk — festival-goers flocking in the thousands towards the main stage to witness a young musical phenomenon from Australia dish out an absolute show-stopper.”
– The Firefly Column, USA

“Daniel Champagne is a crossroads, fusing the strong traditions of blues, folk, and other roots art with pop showmanship and admirable lyrical ability. I firmly believe that he will become an ambassador for roots music in a time where it desperately needs representation.”
– The Indie Blender, Canada

“Reinventing roots guitar.”
– Rhythms Magazine, Australia

“Watching Daniel Champagne perform is a once-in-a-lifetime experience. He is a true prodigy who plays like no one else could possibly play unless they spent at least two lifetimes studying the art.”
– BW Review, New Zealand

Presented by Nightingale Concerts - the listening-room experience


OLD ST PAUL'S is one of Wellington’s most breathtaking and evocative performance spaces, revered for its grandeur, warmth, and extraordinary natural acoustics. Built entirely of native timber, the soaring nave and finely crafted interior create a sound that is rich, resonant, and deeply immersive. The scale of the space offers both intimacy and awe, drawing audiences into a shared listening experience where music lingers and breathes. Designed for seated performances and reverent attention, Old St Paul’s carries a rare stillness — a place where silence feels sacred, dynamics unfold naturally, and every note is given time, space, and meaning.

id: Hanne Jøstensen The Lighthouse Winter Tour | Wellington-311 The Parade, Island Bay, Wellington 6023, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: Hanne Jøstensen The Lighthouse Winter Tour | Wellington
venue: 311 The Parade, Island Bay, Wellington 6023, New Zealand
long_description:
Wellington south coast singer-songwriter Hanne Jøstensen’s delicate and stirring songs carry a beautiful sense of intimacy, stillness and emotional depth. Her intricate second EP ‘The Lighthouse’, released in autumn 2026, reached #10 on the Aotearoa Album chart and spent three weeks in the top 20. Hanne's music navigates her unique upbringing on a tiny Norwegian island (where her grandfather was the lighthouse keeper), woven into modern day life on Aotearoa's wild south coast. She is celebrating the release of 'The Lighthouse' with a winter tour of up-close concerts in the lower north & the south.

“The Lighthouse is a thoughtfully and gracefully composed EP, with moments of breathtaking beauty.” Peter K Malthus, Muzic.nz.

After a booked-out EP launch event in May, Hanne Jøstensen and her team of talented musicians are returning to the architecturally and acoustically beautiful St Hilda's Church in Island Bay, this time as part of the South Coast Arts Trail Wellington. They will also perform songs from Hanne's debut EP 'Watch over me', sprinkled with the occasional cover by artists that have had a significant influence on her songwriting.

After a busy and wonderful weekend at the South Coast Arts Trail, this concert brings us together as a wider community to connect and unwind. It concludes the Arts Trail and Hanne's The Lighthouse 2026 Winter Tour.

Family friendly

Wheelchair accessible

WELCOME!

For more info about the tour or Hanne's music, go to https://linktr.ee/hannejostensen

id: 11 August 2026 Whisky Tasting-16 Dundas Street, Seatoun, Wellington 6022, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: 11 August 2026 Whisky Tasting
venue: 16 Dundas Street, Seatoun, Wellington 6022, New Zealand
long_description:
Whisky Tasting
Tuesday, 11 August 2026
Hosted by John Shearlock from Regional Wines


Join John Shearlock from Regional Wines for another whisky journey at the Seatoun Bowls Club. This time we'll take a look at the history of Scotch whisky as told by 5 drams.

There's a limited release 15-year-old Glenturret (one of Scotland's oldest surviving distilleries), a mystery whisky from a distillery built at the end of the 1800s (the end of whisky's first golden age), a single cask from GlenAllachie (built in the swinging 60s), a cask strength Ardnahoe (which opened in 2019) and a modern 'finished' indie bottling from James Eadie.  Taste 5 fab drams and take a tour through the last 250 years of Scotch whisky history.


Glenturret 15 years old 2024 release 50.8% 

James Eadie  Mannochmore 12 Year Old First Fill PX Sherry Hogshead Finish #378492 52.7%  

GlenAllachie 'Virgin Oak Barrel Single Cask' 2009 / 15 years old #804305 56.9%

Mystery whisky 

Ardnahoe Cask Strength 5YO 60.9%


Tickets are $60 per person and include guided tastings of all the whiskies.

The tasting begins at 7:30pm, so please arrive early to secure a seat, grab a beer, and settle in before we start. Whether you’re a seasoned whisky lover or simply curious to learn more, this promises to be a relaxed and flavour-packed evening. Spaces are limited.

Please contact Kevin or email seatounclubhouse@gmail.com if you'd like to reserve a table for your group.

venue: 172 Cuba Street, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
Road to Beervana is making a pit stop at Cuba Street, and we weren't going to miss it.

We're putting your Thursday knock-off in Cassels' hands, leaving our kitchen to whip up the kai to match, and bringing everyone together for an after-work session with the people behind one of New Zealand's favourite independent breweries.

Four Cassels beers, four matched bites, $40.

Sounds pretty good already... but this isn't four beers lined up beside four snacks with everyone politely agreeing they work. name: [Postponed] City Gallery Wellington Te Whare Toi
venue: 101 Wakefield Street, Wellington Central, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
We have kindly been invited to join NZIQS for an exclusive behind-the-scenes tour of one of Wellington's most significant civic redevelopment projects.

City Gallery Wellington Te Whare Toi is one of New Zealand's leading contemporary art galleries and an iconic civic building located in the heart of Te Ngakau Civic Square. The gallery is currently undergoing a major refurbishment and earthquake strengthening programme as part of Wellington City Council's wider vision to revitalise the Te Ngakau Civic Precinct.

name: Fresh Off The Page: Clay Pigeons
venue: 12 Cambridge Terrace, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
Fresh Off The Page returns to Pōneke with two new play readings from Asian playwrights. Be the first to see these brand new scripts in development, as presented by the best and brightest Te Whanganui-a-Tara talent.

Our first play reading is Clay Pigeons by Nadia Freeman.

A local community faces an influx of sinister invaders: pigeons! An anti-pigeon task force forms to deal with the avian scourge. But how should the committee combat these rats with wings? It's up to the audience to decide in this interactive satirical comedy.

About Nadia:

Nadia Freeman is of Pākehā and Indo-Fijian heritage. Her creative work spans experimental performance, poetry, and theatre. She is the writer of Eat These Words - Kia Mau Festival 2021, Another Universe - Aotearoa International Festival of Arts 2022 and The Girmit which toured festivals across Aotearoa and India. Nadia also hosts poetry music segment Spoken Symphonies on RadioActive.fm, is Chair of the Eastern Artists Connection network for Asian artists and produced the 2024 Taite award winning podcast Eastern Sound Stories.

Nadia is supported in this reading by dramaturg Lynda Chanwai-Earle, director Sameena Zehra and comedy consultant Jerome Chandrahasen. Clay Pigeons features performers Oliver Pol, Phoebe Caldeiro, Elliott Lam, Ralph Johnson, Ocean Manutulila and Jerome Chandrahasen.

About Proudly Asian Theatre
Proudly Asian Theatre aims to connect and empower Asian talent to produce original and contemporary theatre works, to represent, entertain and break down barriers of acceptance and visibility in Aotearoa. Read more here.

Brought to you by Proudly Asian Theatre with support from Copyright Licensing New Zealand and Wellington City Council. Produced by Jess Karamjeet and Cassandra Tse, with assistance from Ayush Aditya.

venue: 12 Cambridge Terrace, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
Poetry by Lisa Maule, music by Michelle Scullion, directed by Jim Moriarty

Theatre-maker Lisa Maule performs her collection of poetry about creativity and questioning.  Poems include commentary about a 'capitalist stapler’, growing up in the hilly suburb of Karori and places of conflicted feelings.  

Not a straight town at all, not a straight down.

An asphalt zigzag.

Home to hydrangea’s, cats, rats, cars, tartan trinkets, china tea cups &

traces of ancient trees."


Embrace unexpected laughs, challenge your norms and immerse yourself in creativity.




REVIEWS

"...it was also about the personal and political sentiment, more than any dazzle with music and rhyme and rhythm and repetition. This was about pure heart." - Simon Sweetman




"The energy buzzing between Lisa and the incredible Michelle Scullion is such a highlight of the show." - Gin Mabey

id: Grass Roots - ONE NIGHT ONLY!-12 Cambridge Terrace, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: Grass Roots - ONE NIGHT ONLY!
venue: 12 Cambridge Terrace, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
“Would you risk it all for the ruck and maul?”


For one night, and one night only, Grass Roots returns to Te Whanganui-a-Tara this TAHI Festival at the iconic Hannah (September 18th)!

Written and performed by Raureti Ormomnd, Grass Roots is a semi-autobiographical musical comedy based on his life as the (very) queer son of a pro rugby player. 


From the club fields to Eden Park, a young man embarks on an odyssey through the New Zealand Rugby Ages. Join him in this historical exploration of queerness, masculinity and the mighty Land of the Long White Cloud. Featuring iconic kiwi hits, you’re in for a ruck-us night! Lace up those cleats… GRASS ROOTS is about to kick off!

This solo theatre show examines the good and the bad of rugby; the machismo and dysfunction, the camaraderie and pride. It unearths the forgotten stories of the game, from the legends of 18th Century Warwickshire to the tales of the 1981 Springbok Tour - and you can’t forget a very important stop in the clubhouse changing room! 

Above all, it speaks to the nature of growing up as takatāpui in a world that doesn’t quite feel like your own. The ultimate catharsis is found within the bond shared by a father and son, who seemingly come from two different worlds, but teach each other the true measure of what it means to be a man.

venue: 33 Bunny Street, Pipitea, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
GEN NZ Unconference and Workshops are back again, and it's all happening at Victoria University of Wellington this year!

This unique opportunity to connect and reconnect will be held on Monday, 24 August (Workshops) and Tuesday, 25 August (Unconference) at Victoria University's Rutherford House.

Let's come together kanohi ki te kanohi / face to face and learn from each other about the art and science of entrepreneurship, and how to improve our entrepreneurial ecosystem. Join your ecosystem colleagues and new ones for a barely controlled explosion of entrepreneurial energy.

The Unconference on Tuesday, 25th August, brings together people from all over the country and the various niches in the entrepreneurial ecosystem to collaborate on how we can connect entrepreneurs to the resources and people they need to thrive, locally and globally. At an unconference, you set the agenda - and we’ll be soliciting ideas for sessions closer to the date. We’ll meet in small groups and discuss topics that are of interest on the day. Everyone can contribute to the conversation, and the main idea is to connect with like-minded people with whom you can work together to achieve your common goals. The Unconference sessions will be facilitated, but there won’t be a single “presenter” as such in the sessions.

The Unconference will be preceded by a day of workshops on Monday, 24th August. The workshop sessions will be more traditional conference workshops - led by one or two people, with presentations, each with specific learning outcomes, and feeding into the Unconference sessions the following day.

Our first announced presenters and workshops include:

James Pinner, NZGCP
Changing Investment Patterns: What the Data Are Telling Us

Mark Bradford, Skills Institute
The Quiet Founder Pipeline: Vocational Learners, Succession, and the Next 200,000 Owner-Operators

Parisa Shademan, Creative Coast
AI Workflows for Non-Technical Entrepreneurs

Dan Thurston Crow, Doso
No Reward Without Risk: Overcoming Fear, Hesitation, and Resistance

Alicia Baxter, IPONZ
From Ideas to Impact: Unlocking the Role of IP in New Zealand’s Productivity Challenge

Wellyforge, Creative HQ, The Atom, Taiawa, and Angel HQ
Revitalising Wellington’s Entrepreneurial Ecosystem

More speakers, workshop details, and agenda updates will be announced soon.

venue: 139 Vivian Street, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
Note: This is an in-person only event at Victoria University of Wellington 139 Vivian Street, Te Aro Campus

About this event:

Dan Bradley has over 19 years’ experience leading complex construction and property projects in New Zealand. In this session, he’ll share practical insights from a seismic strengthening project using the NZS 3910:2023 Target Price model, highlighting collaborative risk management and cost clarity in action.

About the Presenter:

Dan Bradley is the Managing Director of BPM Ltd with 19+ years' experience leading complex construction and property projects across New Zealand. He specialises in project leadership, strategic planning, and client-side representation — from schools and public infrastructure to large-scale commercial builds. Recent highlights include major ongoing developments like the Miramar Golf Club upgrade and food processing facility for Farmland Foods. He’s passionate about transforming construction workflows, an initiative aimed at improving wellbeing in the industry.

Dan’s key strengths are strategic planning, stakeholder engagement, feasibility analysis, and assembling high-performing project teams. He brings a commercial mindset, sharp financial acumen, and deep sector knowledge — always focused on value, clarity, and delivery.

PDU Claim Code:0129202CUV

venue: 3 market lane, Wellington Central, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
At this workshop, FENZ and University of Canterbury will share outcomes of the project “Changing evacuation behaviour to meet densified housing needs for our current and future population”. We’re asking engineers, architects, facility managers and mobility-impaired members of the public for feedback on project outcomes, potential uptake, dissemination, impact and direction.

Continuing Professional Development (CPD)


This workshop provides 3.5 hours of professional development. Participants may be able to record these hours towards their Engineering New Zealand (EngNZ) CPD requirements, subject to CPD obligations.

Attendees can download or print their event ticket (or save it as a PDF) as evidence of attendance. This can be retained as supporting documentation for Continuing Professional Development (CPD) records, where required.

Speakers:

Amy Harpur (FENZ & University of Canterbury)
Wing Yiu Ma (Yoyo), Daniel Nilsson, Peter Thompson (University of Canterbury)

Workshop schedule:

8:30am Arrival, breakfast snacks, coffee & tea          

	

10:30 am Coffee, tea break




9.00 – 10:30 am

Occupant Elevator Evacuations and Areas of Refuge – supporting mobility-impaired occupants

	

10:45 – 12:15 pm
Digital design and simulation tools – free from BIM to Sim




Investigating the needs of mobility impaired building occupants during an emergency evacuation. Towards a multi-disciplinary whole system approach to implementing evacuation lifts and refuge areas in New Zealand buildings.

Project scoping and aims

Experimental methods & outcomes

Operationalising research outcomes for New Zealand buildings

Structured feedback Q&A from attendees

	

Free Software tools for engineers, architects and managers to support and model evacuations of mixed ability populations from buildings: from BIM to simulation and 3D visualisation.

Integrated connection from BIM to B-RISK

Connecting BIM to mixed-ability evacuation modelling and on to 3D animation. How to access the tools.

Suggested workflows for engineers and designers, outcomes from testing

Structured feedback, Q&A from attendees

12:15-12:30 pm Overall review and next steps

Many thanks to our sponsors and supporters:

Friday 18 September 2026
Te Whanganui-a-Tara (Wellington)

We warmly invite you to our 2026 Professional Development Day in Te Whanganui-a-Tara Wellington. It will be a day of connection, learning, and reflection as we look to the future of our profession and fill our kete with new knowledge and understanding.

Event Details

Venue: Rydge's Wellington, 75 Featherston Street (limited parking available, please contact venue)


Date: Friday 18 September 2026

Timing:

Registration opens: 8:00 AM

Gather from: 8:30 AM, 

Programme starts: 9.00 AM

Followed by kōrero and kai until 5:30 PM

Programme Highlights

View the Latest Programme HERE

The PD Workshops Day Programme will be updated regularly on the NZAC website and through our PD Newsletters.

As well as our keynote sessions and workshop, the programme includes:

Morning tea, lunch, and afternoon tea – time to connect with colleagues, NZAC’s National Executive, and National Office staff.

Kaupapa Network Tables – informal lunchtime conversations around shared interests.

Canapés from 4.30 –5.30 pm – a chance to unwind and reconnect with new and old friends.

$250.00 + $37.50 GST + Humanitix fees

Questions

If you have any questions, contact Vanessa-Jayne on pdmanager@nzac.nz or Jo McNab on info@nzac.org.nz

venue: Level 7/86 Victoria Street, Wellington Central, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
Electrify Aotearoa doesn't end when the conference finishes.

Community Connections brings together the Electrify community in regions across Aotearoa, creating more opportunities for wāhine founders to connect, share experiences, and support one another throughout the year.

Because building a great company shouldn't depend on where you live. Together, we're creating more opportunities for women founders to connect, learn, and thrive.

What is it?
This event is all about connecting wāhine founders and building stronger local communities to support each other and your startups.

Why you should come:
We’re bringing founders together to meet, share ideas, and form connections that actually move startups forward. Over one hour - and fueled with snacks and coffee - this is your chance to build new local relationships and shape your next move.

Who should attend?

id: GOVIS AGM 2026-3 Mulgrave Street, Thorndon, Wellington 6011, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: GOVIS AGM 2026
venue: 3 Mulgrave Street, Thorndon, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
The GOVIS AGM will be held from 4.45pm on Thursday September 17th at The Thistle Inn, Wellington (and online). Formalities start from 5pm. Food and drink are provided.

It has been a busy year for GOVIS - we have run Copilot training sessions, and our biggest conference in the post-COVID era, with over 175 people registered and 10 sponsors. We have bedded in our new constitution by developing a members register and confirming many new members and subscribing agencies, partners, and sponsors; and have forged some new ones. Most importantly, we have held true to our core values of helping public servants who work in technology, information, data and AI to connect, share and learn; through what has been a challenging period for many of our members.

At the AGM we will:

Reflect on our successes and challenges in the past year

Agree on our priorities for the year ahead

Vote on our organising committee and officers

Confirm minor ammendments to new constitution from 2025

We will share papers to RSVPed attendees one week in advance of the AGM.

A GOVIS AGM is a lot of fun, so you should definitely come along! It's a chance to get to know the GOVIS committee better and have a chat or to tentatively explore becoming more involved, even if it is just in a small or informal way. Being part of GOVIS is a way give back to our profession - GOVIS events don't just happen by themselves and we need a range of skills to function. Being on the GOVIS committee is also a way to step up and develop yourself. So whether you’re an events pro, finance whiz, project manager with flair, can decipher contracts, are a creative marketing guru, love connecting and learning, or just want to be supporting our kaupapa, then the AGM is the place for you.

Anyone is welcome to attend, but only GOVIS members may stand for the committee and the officer roles (i.e. President, Treasurer and Secretary), and vote on nominations or motions. GOVIS members need to 1) complete the membership form & declaration, and 2) ensure they have paid either as an individual or that their employer is a subscribing agency. For more information, see our membership page here, or contact us here: members@govis.org.nz

If you would like to nominate yourself (or someone else) for the committee or for an officer role (i.e. President, Treasurer, or Secretary), then please the GOVIS Secretary know by Tuesday 15th September. If you would like a motion to be tabled at the AGM please also let the GOVIS Secretary know any time prior to the AGM. You can contact the GOVIS Secretary here: info@govis.org.nz

Logistics:

We are meeting at the Thistle Inn on 3 Mulgrave Street, upstairs in the Georges Room. The room will be ready and food & drink available from 4.45pm, so if you are attending in person please try to arrive at this time so that there is time to get settled in and fed & watered before we begin.

Details for connecting on Microsoft Teams will be sent out prior to the event to everyone who registers for the AGM. If you are attending online you are welcome to join the call any time from 4.45pm, but note that formal proceedings will not begin until around 5.00pm.

long_description:
⭐ CPD Points: 20

Description

This CPD course, titled "Mastering Masterspec Specifications," is designed to provide specifiers with comprehensive training on effectively utilising the Masterspec platform for specification writing. Participants will learn the ins and outs of navigating the Masterspec platform, setting up their specifications, managing user accounts, and optimising the use of various features such as Office Masters, MasterKey, and mDocs. The course covers essential topics ranging from basic specification setup to advanced specification management techniques, ensuring participants gain practical skills to streamline their specification writing process.

Designed by specifiers for specifiers

This course is designed for specifiers, including architects, designers, engineers, and other professionals involved in the construction industry, who are responsible for creating specifications for building projects. Whether you are new to the Masterspec platform or looking to enhance your proficiency in specification writing, this course provides valuable insights and practical skills to optimise your workflow and maximise the benefits of using Masterspec for specification management.

Why should specifiers take this course

Specifiers should take this course to enhance their proficiency in specification writing and maximise the benefits offered by the Masterspec platform. By mastering the tools and functionalities covered in this course, specifiers can:

Improve Efficiency: Learn how to navigate the Masterspec website and utilise its features effectively, saving time and effort in specification writing tasks.
Ensure Accuracy: Gain insights into best practices for setting up specifications, assigning roles, and managing user accounts to maintain data accuracy and consistency.
Enhance Collaboration: Understand how to collaborate with team members, assign roles, and share specifications seamlessly within the organization, promoting teamwork and productivity.
Stay Updated: Stay abreast of the latest features and updates on the Masterspec platform, ensuring specifiers are equipped with the knowledge to leverage new tools for enhanced specification writing.
Optimise Workflow: Discover advanced techniques for managing specifications, utilising Office Masters, and integrating with drawing sets using MasterKey, leading to streamlined workflow and project efficiency.
Ensure Compliance: Learn about NZCIC guidelines and best practices for adding, editing, and exporting guidelines to ensure compliance with industry standards and regulations.
Boost Professional Development: Acquire valuable skills and knowledge that contribute to professional growth and advancement in the field of specification writing, enhancing career prospects and opportunities.

venue: 7 Moncrieff Street, Mount Victoria, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
Grieving Well: a Solution-Focused approach to loss

Trainer: Matt Cameron, MNZCCA

Thursday 20 August

9.30am-4.30pm (6 hours PD)

Quaker Meeting House, 7 Moncrieff Street, Mount Victoria, Wellington

$95

Students and unwaged: $50

Register via the NZCCA website: https://www.nzcca.org.nz/_events.registration/step2/eventid/39584/type/single

Craig will send you an invoice for payment.

or email Silvia at silvia.purdie@gmail.com

From Matt:

My experience of working with grief is that we never “get over” our losses but we can learn to live with them in ways that are helpful and healing. Change can be hard but we can become better and more confident, learning to live with the changes that we experience.

I apply the Solution Focused approach to all my work.

The Solution Focused Approach is currently a leading method around the world in leadership, coaching, social work and counselling. I believe it is simple and easy to apply, which means you will gain skills and knowledge that can immediately apply to your situation. The Solution Focused approach can be described as a client-centred, strength-based, multi-cultural and user-friendly style that is life changing and applicable to every situation. Come on a journey of change, joy and possibility.

 

Matt Cameron has trained and worked in both teaching and counselling, specialising in grief and loss. He has been working in South Canterbury as the Oceans Grief and Loss Coordinator since 2012. He is also one of Aotearoa’s leading proponents and trainers of the Solution Focused approach for the past decade. He enjoys various sports and has played competitive tennis, badminton, soccer, rugby and most recently fistball. Based in Timaru, Matt co-ordinates the Online Region of the NZ Christian Counsellors Association.

Discover Solutions: https://discoversolutions.nz/

Training provided by the Wellington Region of the NZ Christian Counsellors Association. Supported by Silvia Purdie, Conversations Seminars

https://www.conversationscounselling.nz/seminars.html

long_description:
Grieving Well: a Solution-Focused approach to loss

Trainer: Matt Cameron, MNZCCA

Thursday 20 August

9.30am-4.30pm (6 hours PD)

Quaker Meeting House, 7 Moncrieff Street, Mount Victoria, Wellington

Students and unwaged: $50

or email Silvia at silvia.purdie@gmail.com

From Matt:

My experience of working with grief is that we never “get over” our losses but we can learn to live with them in ways that are helpful and healing. Change can be hard but we can become better and more confident, learning to live with the changes that we experience.

I apply the Solution Focused approach to all my work.

The Solution Focused Approach is currently a leading method around the world in leadership, coaching, social work and counselling. I believe it is simple and easy to apply, which means you will gain skills and knowledge that can immediately apply to your situation. The Solution Focused approach can be described as a client-centred, strength-based, multi-cultural and user-friendly style that is life changing and applicable to every situation. Come on a journey of change, joy and possibility.

 

Matt Cameron has trained and worked in both teaching and counselling, specialising in grief and loss. He has been working in South Canterbury as the Oceans Grief and Loss Coordinator since 2012. He is also one of Aotearoa’s leading proponents and trainers of the Solution Focused approach for the past decade. He enjoys various sports and has played competitive tennis, badminton, soccer, rugby and most recently fistball. Based in Timaru, Matt co-ordinates the Online Region of the NZ Christian Counsellors Association.

Discover Solutions: https://discoversolutions.nz/

Training provided by the Wellington Region of the NZ Christian Counsellors Association. Supported by Silvia Purdie, Conversations Seminars

id: Breathwork & Sound Odyssey with Saxon-18 Manners Street, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: Breathwork & Sound Odyssey with Saxon
venue: 18 Manners Street, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
Breathwork & Sound Odyssey
With Saxon
Friday 28th August

Inspired by the wild coastline of Wainuiomata, where the golden light of sunset meets the rhythm of the sea, Saxon spent countless hours drumming in deep connection with the wairua of the land.

This journey is also shaped by the mystery of the Orongorongo Forests, where many days were spent immersed beneath the canopy, listening and responding to the pulse of the natural world through rhythm and presence.

These landscapes have become part of Saxon’s musical language.

Instruments

Saxon will weave multiple instruments & soundscapes throughout this immersive sound journey, each carrying its own unique energy.

Her most treasured instrument is her drum—a handcrafted frame drum from Bali. While the instrument itself originates from Indonesia, Saxon's connection to drumming is deeply inspired by her Swedish ancestry and the ancient traditions of northern Scandinavia, where drums were revered as sacred instruments by the Indigenous Sámi people for ceremony, spiritual guidance, and connection with the natural world. She honours these traditions with humility and respect, using rhythm as a way to cultivate presence, reverence, and a deeper relationship with the land.

Together, the drum and voice create a space where the body can soften, the spirit can listen, and the heart can remember.

Sound Odyssey is an immersive experience woven from these places—a soundscape that invites you into both mystery and presence, stillness and movement.

Agenda

The evening begins with a gentle guided breathwork practice. As an accredited breathwork and somatic facilitator, Saxon will guide the group through simple breathing techniques to help regulate the nervous system, settle into the body, and arrive fully in the present moment before the sound journey begins.

Details

Friday 28th August

Breathwork & Sound Odyssey

With Saxon

$30 per person

12 spaces only

Accessibility
Please note that this venue is located in a basement and does not have wheelchair access.

If accessibility prevents you from attending this event, stay tuned—the next Sound Odyssey will be held in a wheelchair-accessible venue.

What to Bring

Please bring anything you need to make your experience as comfortable and nurturing as possible.

We recommend wearing comfortable clothing and bringing a yoga mat, cushion, blanket, and an eye mask or blindfold if you have one. You are welcome to lie down or sit in a meditation posture throughout the journey.

Most importantly, listen to your body and choose whatever feels right for you. This is your experience, and you are encouraged to settle into a position that allows you to feel safe, supported, and at ease.

A note on safety and self-responsibility
These experiences are offered as a space for connection, reflection, and embodied exploration. Each participant is responsible for honouring their own physical, emotional, and psychological boundaries. Please seek professional guidance before attending if you have a history of psychosis, schizophrenia, mania, or any mental health condition that may be impacted by deep meditation, breathwork, sound immersion, or altered states of consciousness.

By joining us, you acknowledge that you are choosing to participate voluntarily and take responsibility for your own wellbeing throughout the experience.

Any questions, please feel free to contact Saxon via email

id: Grey Not Blue: Depression and suicide in older people - Te Whanganui-a-Tara - Wellington (GNB2026/07)-2 Rhine Street, Island Bay, Wellington 6023, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: Grey Not Blue: Depression and suicide in older people - Te Whanganui-a-Tara - Wellington (GNB2026/07)
venue: 2 Rhine Street, Island Bay, Wellington 6023, New Zealand
long_description:
Take the opportunity to learn more about suicide in older people, the forgotten population in mental wellbeing and suicide prevention

There are some suicide risk factors that are particular to older people yet rarely are included in suicide risk assessment tools nor covered in suicide prevention training.

Many general population suicide prevention and mental wellbeing campaigns do not or inadequately address the unique contributing factors to depression and suicide in older people.

Studies indicate that the aged care sector is underprepared, the workforce under skilled and there lacks leadership to champion effective prevention strategies and promoting wellbeing in older people.

It is critical that those working with older people are:

knowledgeable about the latest research and understanding of suicide in older people

confident and competent in responding to the depressed or suicidal older person

Suicide in the over-65 age group is more prevalent than commonly understood. Recent statistics indicate a rising trend in suicide among the elderly. Often under-reported, depression and suicide are significant mental health concerns for this demographic.

An emerging mental health concern for Retirement Villages and Aged Care Facilities

As the baby boomer generation ages, many will enjoy reasonable physical health. However mental health issues particularly depression will become more prevalent. This is not just a concern for primary care or aged care facilities but requires serious consideration by management and staff in retirement villages. A study of suicide locations in New Zealand found that aged care facilities and retirement villages were the most common places where older people killed themselves. This has implications for family, staff and other residents.

Older People Suicide vs Assisted Dying

An understanding of the distinction between assisted dying and suicidality in older people is crucial for those working with older people. The workshop will cover the complex interrelationship of factors the between suicidality and assisted dying.

TAYLORMADE TRAINING AND CONSULTING IS PROUD TO BE AN AGE CONCERN DIGNITY CHAMPION - TAKING A STAND AGAINST AGEISM & PROMOTING POSITIVE AGEING

id: Awakening the Subtle Body with Joan Hyman-Level 1/175 Vivian Street, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: Awakening the Subtle Body with Joan Hyman
venue: Level 1/175 Vivian Street, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
About the training

This immersive training invites you to awaken the subtle body through the practice of yoga. The subtle body is the energetic field that connects body, breath and mind.

Over the course of this 3-day training, we explore how movement, breath and awareness shape the flow of prana. Through asana, pranayama and meditation, you will deepen your connection to the more subtle layers of your practice and refine how you move, breathe and sequence with intention.

What you will explore

The foundations of yoga energetics including prana, nadis, bandhas and chakras

the relationship between physical alignment and the energetic flow

Sequencing as a tool to guide prana through the body

Pranayama and meditation as gateways to the subtle body

Safe and intelligent progressions toward more advanced postures

Any questions? Head to our FAQ at the bottom of the page.

SCHEDULE

The training is 3 full days with each day designed to lead on to the next. Lunch break is from 12-1:30pm.

Friday 9am - 4pm - Sequencing towards arm balances

We explore sequencing as a roadmap for practice and learn how arm balances support lightness, strength and flow. Themes include prana, the five koshas, bandhas and biomechanics as a gateway to the subtle body. The day ends with pranayama practice.

Saturday 9am - 4pm - Sequencing towards inversions and inner body awareness

A deeper exploration of inversions and their effect on the inner body. We study the nadis and sushumna and how sequencing supports inward awareness. The day closes with restorative postures and meditation.

Sunday 9am - 3:30pm - Sequencing for backbends and subtle body integration

Backbends to uplift prana and access the more subtle layers of practice. We will explore the chakras as the most refined energetic layer and integrate everything through sequencing, meditation, and pranayama. A quiet inward ending to conclude the training.

THE VENUE: BHAKTI LOUNGE

The Bhakti Lounge is located in the heart of Wellington CBD, at level 1, 175 Vivian Street. It has been operating for twenty plus years and is 100% volunteer-run, community first events space.

YOUR TEACHER

Joan Hyman, Senior Yoga Teacher and founder of the School of Yoga (USA)

Joan Hyman is the director and founder of The School of Yoga, an authentic international teacher training program focused on continuing education. Her grounded teaching style seamlessly supports her students as they emerge from their practice with the rich and bright energy that yoga has to offer.

Joan’s teachings come from an organic and intuitive place, as she draws upon the combined studies of Ashtanga and Iyengar yoga as well as Ayurveda and meditation. An authentic modern-day yogi, Joan's love and devotion show up in her practice and throughout her teaching. You will leave her class feeling transformed and deeply aligned.

Joan spent fifteen years as a distinguished YogaWorks Senior Teacher before bringing her expertise to Wanderlust as the Director of Teacher Trainings in 2016. Now, with over twenty years of experience leading retreats, trainings, and international workshops, Joan travels the globe and teaches online, leading her own signature trainings. She has created The School of Yoga, which is a professional education program, helping students and inspiring teachers to work towards their five hundred hours Yoga Alliance Certification. A leader in the yoga community, Joan’s open-hearted approach to teaching yoga keeps both her inner spirit and her students continuously evolving.

YOUR HOSTS

Sarah Marriott and Liz Birkett

Yoga teachers (500YTT) Sarah Marriott and Liz Birkett warmly welcome you! Having studied with Joan Hyman since 2018, they are excited to bring her to Wellington shores once again, so she can share her extensive knowledge of Yoga with Aotearoa's Yoga community. 

FAQ

How much is the 3 day training?

It is $520 (early bird) however this increases to $550 from November 1st, 2026.

Can I attend one or two days?

Sorry, no. This is a 3 day training with each day designed to lead on to the next. Please email Sarah and Liz if you have further questions about this.

Who is this training for?

This training is for dedicated practitioners and teachers who feel curious about the energetics behind the physical practice and who want to deepen their experience beyond alignment alone. This training is open to teachers and dedicated yoga practitioners. You do not need to be a teacher to join. A regular yoga practice and curiosity to dive deeper is enough!

Do I need to bring a yoga mat or any props?

We have mats, and props (blocks, straps bolsters) however you are welcome to bring your own.

Is there parking at the venue?

Street parking:
Best option is to Uber or car pool if you can as street parking is capped at 2 hours (around $5 per hour) during the week and 3 hours (around $3/4) in the weekend.

Car parks:
The Hope Gibbons Parking (68 Taranaki Street) is a 2-3 minute walk from the venue or there are other parking buildings 5 minutes away (E.g., Garrett Street Car Park)

What are the lunch options?

Of course you are welcome to bring your own lunch/snacks. However, there are plenty of cafes and restaurants available to you on nearby Cuba street. You have 1.5 hours for lunch so you may like to dine in, take a drive or head to Oriental Pde for a walk!

The Bhakti lounge also serves a delicious plant-based lunch Mon-Fri at a very affordable price.

I'm from out of town. Is there accommodation nearby?

Yes there are plenty of options just a short walk away.

name: TŪ TOA 2026: Creating Māori Success in Education
venue: 53 Waiapu Road, Karori, Wellington 6012, New Zealand
long_description:
Education has always been one of the most powerful vehicles for Māori advancement. Across generations, Māori have drawn on mātauranga Māori, whānau aspirations, innovation, leadership and determination to create transformative educational success.

From kōhanga reo and kura kaupapa Māori, to wānanga, schools, tertiary institutions, research organisations and community-led initiatives, Māori continue to reimagine what educational excellence can look like in Aotearoa and beyond.

Tū Toa 2026 brings together an outstanding group of Māori and allied education leaders to explore a critical question: How do we create Māori success in education in the next decade? Through keynote presentations and interactive wānanga, participants will examine proven models of success, emerging opportunities, contemporary challenges and the leadership required to create transformational outcomes for future generations.

Together, we will identify the insights, principles and practices that can strengthen educational achievement across whānau, hapū, iwi, communities and institutions.

This conference is more than a professional development event. It is an opportunity to contribute to the future of Māori education and to the wider nation-building journey of Aotearoatanga.

As knowledge has been passed from generation to generation, so too must we gather, share and apply the wisdom of today's educational leaders. Join us as we celebrate Māori success, strengthen educational leadership, and help shape the next chapter of educational transformation in Aotearoa New Zealand.

Confirmed Speakers
• Evie O'Brien – Chief Executive Officer, Te Wānanga o Aotearoa
• Kaapua Smith – Partner, KPMG
• Dr Peggy Burrows – Principal, Haeata Community Campus, Christchurch
• Dr Mahinaarangi Baker – Managing Director, Te Kōnae, TWOR;
• Dr Areti Metuamate – Master and Head, Ormond College, University of Melbourne;
• Dr Alex Barnes, Te Rau Ora, Te Rau Rangahau Manager;
• Anika Edginton – Wellington NZ.


MC's

Kara Nepe-Apatu and Elena Higgison


Tū Toa 2026 is hosted by:
Kathie Irwin and Associates  and The Mana Wahine Foundation (Registered NZ Charity). Any proceeds from the conference will be donated to The Mana Wahine Foundation to further its charitable purposes.

We can't wait to celebrate all that God has done in and through The Salvation Army Miramar over the past 100 years! As part of our celebration weekend happening on 15-16 August, you're invited to a delicious dinner together on Saturday 15th from 5.30pm.

This will be an evening of kai, connection and entertainment. We have a delicious catered dinner and dessert lined up, along with live music, interactive moments and celebration, and devotions from a past Miramar icon.

Book your seat at the big Miramar Celebration feast - it will be a great evening for all ages together!

Venue and meal info:

Our evening together is at Ākau Tangi Sports Centre in Kilbirnie (previously ASB Sports Centre). We will be based upstairs in the Mātairangi room - there is lift access to this area. Ākau Tangi has a large amount of free parking onsite.

The meal is catered onsite and includes a main meal of protein, vegetables, bread and salad, as well as dessert - delish! (You can note dietary requirements when booking).

Ticket info:

While the rest of our the weekend's schedule is free/no booking required, our celebration feast dinner requires tickets to help cover some of the cost of the meal and help the caterers prepare enough kai for us all! Miramar Salvation Army is subsidising each ticket to make this more accessible for everyone.

Adult: $25 per person
Children 5-14 years: $12 per person
Under 5s: no cost

If you'd like to contribute more towards the cost of the evening or 'sponsor a seat' - you can find these options when you go to select tickets. Thank you!

We don't want ticketing/cost to be a barrier for anyone so we have planned ways to make this possible for people - please reach out - we'd love for you to be there.

We can't wait to see you on the 15-16 August!

For queries, please contact: miramar.corps@salvationarmy.org.nz

For info for the full weekend, see here: https://miramarsalvationarmy.co.nz/100-years/

id: TŪ TOA 2026: Creating Māori Success in Education-53 Waiapu Road, Karori, Wellington 6012, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: TŪ TOA 2026: Creating Māori Success in Education
venue: 53 Waiapu Road, Karori, Wellington 6012, New Zealand
long_description:
Education has always been one of the most powerful vehicles for Māori advancement. Across generations, Māori have drawn on mātauranga Māori, whānau aspirations, innovation, leadership and determination to create transformative educational success.

From kōhanga reo and kura kaupapa Māori, to wānanga, schools, tertiary institutions, research organisations and community-led initiatives, Māori continue to reimagine what educational excellence can look like in Aotearoa and beyond.

Tū Toa 2026 brings together an outstanding group of Māori and allied education leaders to explore a critical question: How do we create Māori success in education in the next decade? Through keynote presentations and interactive wānanga, participants will examine proven models of success, emerging opportunities, contemporary challenges and the leadership required to create transformational outcomes for future generations.

Together, we will identify the insights, principles and practices that can strengthen educational achievement across whānau, hapū, iwi, communities and institutions.

This conference is more than a professional development event. It is an opportunity to contribute to the future of Māori education and to the wider nation-building journey of Aotearoatanga.

As knowledge has been passed from generation to generation, so too must we gather, share and apply the wisdom of today's educational leaders. Join us as we celebrate Māori success, strengthen educational leadership, and help shape the next chapter of educational transformation in Aotearoa New Zealand.

Confirmed Speakers
• Evie O'Brien – Chief Executive Officer, Te Wānanga o Aotearoa
• Kaapua Smith – Partner, KPMG
• Dr Peggy Burrows – Principal, Haeata Community Campus, Christchurch
• Dr Mahinaarangi Baker – Managing Director, Te Kōnae, TWOR;
• Dr Areti Metuamate – Master and Head, Ormond College, University of Melbourne;
• Dr Alex Barnes, Te Rau Ora, Te Rau Rangahau Manager;
• Anika Edginton – Wellington NZ.


MC's

Kara Nepe-Apatu and Elena Higgison


Tū Toa 2026 is hosted by:
Kathie Irwin and Associates  and The Mana Wahine Foundation (Registered NZ Charity). Any proceeds from the conference will be donated to The Mana Wahine Foundation to further its charitable purposes.

SPONSORED BY: TE WĀNANGA O AOTEAROA.

Tū Toa 2026 – Creating Māori Success in Education

Celebrating excellence. Sharing knowledge. Building the future.

Registration opens from 8.30am

Coffee and muffins available on arrival

Start time 9am - Finishing at 5pm

name: Spring for Kaibosh
venue: 167 Riddiford Street, Newtown, Wellington 6021, New Zealand
long_description:
Spring for Kaibosh – musical fundraiser

DJs, dancing and doing good.

Dress up, get down to Moon and boogie all night while helping Kaibosh Food Rescue feed those in our communities that need it most.

Don’t miss this fantastic fundraiser with stellar DJs spinning all night, lights and visuals from the legendary Cubeman and Metrokorg, and sweet sounds powered by Torque Sounds.

House, breaks, tech house, techno, minimal, rave, bass music and more, with good times guaranteed.

Raffle, plus spot prizes for the best dressed (costume theme: spring!).

All proceeds from ticket sales and raffle go straight to Kaibosh Food Rescue. If you can’t make it, you can donate or become a supporter via the Kaibosh website.

Under 18s must be accompanied by a legal guardian.

DJs

Flatmate Dance Therapy record label head Flatmate (aka yourFlatmate) has a playful curiosity for music, a passion for storytelling and an infectious energy whether behind the decks, in the studio or on the dancefloor. He builds worlds rich in story and sonic diversity, capturing the warmth of the past while exploring the progressive endeavours of the present. (@flatmate__ and @dancetherapyrecords on Insta)

Nam Chucks b2B Amira Nam and Amira possess a deep appreciation and respect for Soundsystem philosophy, dedicating their musical selections to the concepts of unity, inclusivity and respect for all sounds sacred and indigenous. Join these two empowered wāhine through sounds of their diaspora. (@nam_chucks on Insta)

Hexadecimal Emerging from the UK underground breakbeat scene in the early 2000s, Scott Reeder quickly established himself as an internationally respected DJ and producer. With 150+ releases to his name and two albums on Distinctive Records, his output has helped shape a generation of forward-thinking club music.

Now based in New Zealand, Hexadecimal remains highly active, delivering genre-blending, dancefloor-driven DJ sets that reflect both his deep roots and global perspective. (@hexadecimalmusic on Insta)

Ché D Ngāmotu New Plymouth–based visual artist and musician/producer Ché Rogers, aka DJ Ché D, weaves stylish minimal house and techno tunes. Shaken, not stirred, he blends underground classics, originals, and live-improvised remixes with a serving of indie and goth condiments. (@che_rogers_art on Insta)

Lowli Event co-organiser Laurie and his DJ sets are, in a word, FUN! He’s guaranteed to get carried away and bring anyone, and everyone, on the dancefloor with him. (@lowli_dj on Insta)

The Village Idiot Longtime Kaibosh supporter, Lee Slater, has been hogging house-party stereos, and sound systems, for over 20 years. Lee loves flowing, bouncy tunes with a little bit of wonkiness. (@teambenter on Insta)

DJ Danger Ange has been dishing up tasty tunes around Pōneke for the past decade. Expect an eclectic, genre-bending collection of tunes in her vinyl-only set. (@danger.ange.danger on Insta)

VJs & sound

Cubeman VJ Cubeman is an established New Zealand visual artist and live media technician dedicated to turning sound into immersive light environments. Specialising in architectural projection mapping and live video manipulation, Cubeman captures and remixes real-world music moments into what he terms 'the new'.

If you’re not familiar with his work prepare to have your minds blown! (@vjcubeman on Insta)

Metrokorg A frequent partner-in-pixels with Cubeman, Kane is a dedicated champion of the underground scene, actively supporting tech crews and behind-the-scenes production. His VJing, custom projection mapping and immersive mood lighting have helped craft hypnotic visual environments for major festivals and events including Bloom, CubaDupa, Sunny Side Up and numerous Kāpiti gigs. (@metrokorg on Insta)

We’re stoked that this epic event will be POWERED BY TORQUE SOUNDS – Pōneke’s brilliant, custom-built Tub’s Audio sound system. (@torque_sounds on Insta)

See you on the dancefloor…

To find out more about Kaibosh Food rescue and the fantastic work they do, click here.

name: An Evening with Alexander Hillary - Adventure, Legacy and Creating Change in Nepal
venue: 38 Vivian Street, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
Velocity Financial are delighted to invite you to a special fundraising event on Thursday 20 August, featuring Alexander Hillary — adventurer, conservationist, General Manager of the Himalayan Trust, and grandson of Sir Edmund Hillary. Alex is a remarkable person with a remarkable heritage. In this inspiring and thought-provoking evening, he will share stories from his own adventures, reflect on the legacy of his grandfather, and discuss the ongoing work of the Himalayan Trust in Nepal. The Himalayan Trust was founded by Sir Edmund Hillary and Louise Hillary following the first ascent of Everest. More than sixty years later, the organisation continues to support education, healthcare and sustainable community development in some of Nepal's most remote regions. This event will be valuable for anyone interested in:

The legacy of Sir Edmund Hillary and his family

Adventure, exploration and the outdoors

Philanthropy and the impact sector

Leadership, purpose and creating positive change

Nepal and its communities

More information can be found on The Velocity Website - https://www.velocityfinancial.co.nz/event/an-evening-with-alexander-hillary

Velocity Financial are proud to be hosting this event alongside Kaitiaki Foundation and Caveo to help raise awareness and support for the Himalayan Trust. All proceeds from ticket sales will be donated directly to the Trust.

Join us on Friday, 28 August 2026 at 5:30 PM at Newlands College for TEDxPaparangiYouth 2026, an evening of inspiration, creativity, and ideas that challenge us to look beyond the boundaries of today.

Centered around the theme "Limitless Horizons," this year's event explores the possibilities that emerge when we dare to think bigger, dream further, and embrace new perspectives. Through a series of engaging TEDx talks, speakers from a variety of backgrounds will share stories, experiences, and ideas that inspire innovation, resilience, and positive change.

Throughout the evening, attendees will enjoy live performances, opportunities to connect with members of the community, and a selection of food and refreshments. What makes TEDxPaparangiYouth special is its commitment to empowering youth voices while fostering meaningful conversations across generations. By creating a platform where ideas can be shared openly, we hope to inspire attendees to explore new horizons in their own lives, communities, and futures.

Whether you are a student, educator, professional, entrepreneur, artist, or lifelong learner, TEDxPaparangiYouth 2026 offers an opportunity to discover fresh ideas, meet inspiring people, and be part of a community that believes in the power of possibility.

id: Good Company to Listen, Share and Connect-Shop 234, Level 1, Left Bank, 116 Cuba Street, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: Good Company to Listen, Share and Connect
venue: Shop 234, Level 1, Left Bank, 116 Cuba Street, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
Life feels a little better in good company!

We'd love to invite you to join us for an evening of genuine conversation, thoughtful reflection, and meaningful connection in a warm and welcoming space.


The idea behind Good Company

We believe, there is something special about sitting down with good people, sharing stories, listening with curiosity, and leaving feeling a little more connected than when you walked in.

This isn't about having the right answers or trying to fix one another. It's about slowing down, being ourselves, sharing different perspectives, reflecting together, and simply enjoying being in good company.

Each gathering explores a different aspect of everyday life through thoughtful conversation, offering a chance to hear how the same topic can resonate differently with each person in the room.

The topic for this evening is:
"Sense of Belonging"



What to expect

We'll welcome you with a hot cup of tea or coffee and some light snacks before settling in together.

The evening will be gently guided with a few conversation prompts, while leaving plenty of space for the conversation to unfold naturally. There isn't a speaker and there isn't an audience. The conversation belongs to all of us, and every person who joins helps shape the evening.

As a special touch, you're welcome to bring something that connects with the theme. It could be an object, a photograph, a favourite book, a poem, a piece of music, or anything else that holds meaning for you. You're welcome to share the story behind it, or simply keep it with you during the evening.

If this feels like your kind of evening, we'd love to welcome you.


To keep the gathering personal and conversational, places are limited to 8 participants.


Before you book


• This is a space for conversation and connection rather than advice or support.


• It isn't therapy, peer support, crisis support, or a self help group.


• It isn't a place for political or religious advocacy or debate.


• Everyone is invited to participate in whatever way feels comfortable. These evenings are at their best when we each bring a little curiosity, a willingness to listen and be a part of the conversation.


• Please let us know in advance if you have any accessibility requirements or dietary needs, and we'll do our best to accommodate you.

• The ticket fee helps cover the basic costs of running the event. If you're experiencing financial difficulties, please get in touch without hesitation.


• Doors open at 4:00 pm

id: Expand Pōneke | Wellington histories in Wikipedia-65 Victoria Street, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: Expand Pōneke | Wellington histories in Wikipedia
venue: 65 Victoria Street, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
Wikipedia is one of the most-visited websites on the internet, and is a go-to resource for both people and artificial intelligence platforms. Wikipedia articles are kept reliable and up-to-date by thousands of volunteers across the world, but there’s always more to be done. If you’ve ever read a Wikipedia article that was missing some important context, or looked up a topic that didn’t even have an article at all, then now’s your chance to fix it.

Focusing on local histories, the workshop aims to improve coverage of mana whenua (local Māori people) and sites of significance from across Pōneke | Wellington. This three hour session will introduce you to both editing Wikipedia and the amazing history collections at Te Matapihi ki Te Ao Wellington Central Library.

The session is coordinated by Wellingtonian Lisa Maule, Vice President of Wikimedia Aotearoa New Zealand and supported by staff from Te Matapihi ki te Ao Nui | Wellington Central Library and Wellington City Archives.

When: Saturday 31 October, 12:30pm – 3:30pm

Where: Wellington Central Library – Ngā Pou Ruahine 

How: Register for free on Humanitix

Please bring a laptop or tablet and charger. Afternoon tea will be provided. 

The workshop is an ‘edit-a-thon’ where a group of people focuses on adding edits to Wikipedia and the sister projects Wikimedia Commons and Wikidata.

How to prepare for the Wikipedia workshop

For this project we are going to explore adding information about Māori history and pā sites to existing articles. Feel free to review the Wikipedia project page to see what areas of interest you have (w.wiki/RuJ$).  

For beginners there are a few small things you can do in advance.

Important: Please create a Wikipedia account prior to the workshop. You’ll need to create a username and password. We recommend a username that doesn’t include your real name, and is anonymous. While adding an email is optional, we recommend this as it’s very helpful if you forget your password. 

Watching some short videos to introduce you to Wikipedia editing will help you get stuck right in on the day. Our friends at Wikimedia Australia have some great guidance – there’s even one to help you create your account: wikimedia.org.au/wiki/Training

This event is a collaboration between the Te Mataphi ki Te Ao Wellington Central Library, Wellington City Archives, Wikimedia Aotearoa New Zealand (WANZ) and Wellington Heritage Festival.

Step into the magic of Moonlit Memories, Viet Hub NZ’s Moon Festival, where Vietnamese traditions come alive through music, food, crafts, and community.

Tết Trung Thu, also known as the Vietnamese Moon Festival, is one of Vietnam’s most cherished celebrations. It is a festival of family, children, lanterns, mooncakes, and togetherness. Whether you grew up celebrating Trung Thu or are discovering this beautiful tradition for the first time, everyone is welcome to experience the warmth and joy of Vietnamese culture.

Bring your whānau and friends for a day filled with vibrant performances, a traditional Lion Dance, hands-on craft activities, delicious Vietnamese food, interactive cooking workshops, cultural games, and fun for all ages. id: Building Bridges: The New Zealand Vocational Education and Training Research Forum 2026-55 Cable Street, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: Building Bridges: The New Zealand Vocational Education and Training Research Forum 2026
venue: 55 Cable Street, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
Ngā mihi nui!

Skills Group and BCITO are thrilled to join forces again to host the 20th edition of NZVETRF - Building Bridges


Since 2004, the NZVETRF has been the must-attend professional event for policy makers, researchers and practitioners engaged in vocational education, across all parts of the education sector and industry.

NZVETRF will again bring international and national keynote presentations, government and private sector perspectives and education and industry collaboration to the stage.

In 2026, the sector is bedding in further reform, with new players, new structure, new technology and new challenges. Building Bridges is about the critical relationships and collaboration that will make that effective.

Places are limited - register now to secure your place at Aotearoa's pre-eminent cross-sector vocational education event.



Call for Abstracts

	

We now invite submissions from prospective presenters at NZVETRF 2026.

We welcome policy makers, researchers, and practitioners to present evidence-based research and insights to the Forum.

In keeping with the theme of Building Bridges, the abstracts panel will prioritise presentations that demonstrate collaboration between different parts of the system: educators and employers, public and private sectors, secondary and tertiary education...to name a few.

Click here to access the submission form

The call for abstracts closes at 5pm, Friday August 28.




Confirmed Speakers
Dr Tom Bewick
Editor-in-Chief: The Skills Agenda
Visiting Professor of Skills and Workforce Policy, Staffordshire University, UK.


Tom Bewick is a British educationist, consultant, policy adviser, workforce policy journalist, academic and professional career interim at CEO level. He has 35 years of experience working at the forefront of post-compulsory education and training policy and practice, initially as a post-16 adviser to the UK government, between 1997 and 2002; and latterly in both the UK domestic and international arena.



As CEO to five boards since 2004, Tom Bewick has been responsible for several high-profile initiatives. He was the architect of the UK-wide sector skills councils (2001-2010); and he represented the UK awarding bodies for 5 years (2018-2023), securing changes to apprenticeship assessment and qualifications reform.

As visiting professor of skills and workforce policy at the University of Staffordshire, Professor Bewick has recently completed writing an academic book: ‘Skills Policy in Britain and The Future of Work’, published by Bristol University Press/Policy Press on 29th October 2025. He is the author of a number of reports and articles, exploring apprenticeships, skills and productivity. 

Dr Caroline Smith

Dr Caroline Smith is Executive Director of the Centre for Education and Training at Australian Industry Group. She leads the Centre's thought leadership, research and advocacy agenda, advancing industry-informed solutions that strengthen Australia's education and training system, address skills challenges and support a productive, future-ready workforce.

 

With a distinguished career in skills, employment and economic policy, Caroline is recognised for her expertise in workforce development, labour markets, skills systems and workforce planning. She is a strong advocate for collaboration between industry, government and the education sector to deliver workforce and skills solutions that support productivity, economic growth and opportunity.

 

Her previous roles include inaugural Executive Director of Jobs Queensland, Deputy Chief Executive of the National Employment Services Association, and Executive Director, Economic and Policy Futures in the Queensland Department of State Development, Manufacturing, Infrastructure and Planning.

 

Caroline has worked in Australia and internationally on workforce and skills policy and was awarded an Australian-American Fulbright Scholarship in vocational education and training. She joined Australian Industry Group in 2024.

 

Stay tuned for further programme details and speaker announcements.

Your Co-Hosts:

Skills Group operates Skills Trades Training and Skills Institute. We support 17,000 learners and training across 33 industries, through both work-based and provider-based learning, across 15 campuses nationwide.


BCITO is New Zealand's largest provider of Apprenticeships, having qualified 55,000 tradies and counting, across 15 construction and allied trades.

Thank you to our Event Supporters


Sponsor Us!

NZVETRF is a uniquely pan-sector and cross industry event, and we welcome parters, sponsors and supporters from industry and education alike. Our prospectus is here and please contact nzvetrf@skills-group.org for any enquiries.

Confirmed Speakers Dr Tom Bewick Editor-in-Chief: The Skills Agenda Visiting Professor of Skills and Workforce Policy, Staffordshire University, UK.
He has 35 years of experience working at the forefront of post-compulsory education and training policy and practice, initially as a post-16 adviser to the UK government, between 1997 and 2002; and latterly in both the UK domestic and international arena.
