name: AI for schools face-to-face workshop - Wellington
venue: 147 The Terrace, Wellington Central, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
We are offering this in-person AI workshop in Wellington which is designed to support both practical classroom use and school-wide strategic planning, suitable for principals, board members, and teachers.

3 September: Developing an AI-Ready Digital Strategy for Your School
Best for: Principals, board members, senior leaders
Focus: Strategy, governance, risk and responsible adoption

This workshop is designed for principals and senior leaders who want to move beyond general interest in AI and develop a clearer plan for school-wide adoption.

Participants will leave with:

A clear understanding of the opportunities, limitations and risks of AI in school contexts

Knowledge of the board’s role in the governance of technology, including AI in schools or kura

Hands-on experience with AI tools and their applications for school management and governance

A draft framework for a digital strategy incorporating the ethical and legal use of AI tools

Greater confidence and clarity in governing and managing digital strategy and AI adoption

What attendees say:

"We thoroughly enjoyed our day with Dr. Rod Lane learning about AI strategy planning and policy. He provided an incredible amount of valid, essential information that has given us the perfect foundation to begin implementing AI at our school. Dr. Lane was extremely helpful, highly knowledgeable, and took the time to answer all of our questions. We highly recommend his expertise to any educational institution looking to navigate the future of AI safely and strategically. Tina Anderson and Molly Porter - Rototuna Primary School

Please note that all prices are listed per person.

If you have any questions, please contact Innovation@govhub.org.nz.

name: Jewellery Workshops - Spring 2026

long_description:
Join Coveted Jewellery's exclusive workshop in Wellington.

More winter workshop dates to be added 

Design your own sterling silver ring. In just a couple of hours, you’ll go from inspiration to creation, designing and carving your very own wax ring or pendant model. Our experienced jewellers will be there to guide you through every step, whether you're a first-timer or a seasoned artist. Once your wax design is complete, we’ll take care of casting and finishing it in sterling silver, and courier to your doorstep in 4 to 6 weeks.

Quotes to upgrade to gold or add a gemstone are available on the day.

Estimates for casting in gold are calculated based on the weight of your wax model and the current gold price.  Accurate estimates cannot be given out prior to the workshop. Gold prices are subject to change.

Unfortunately we cannot set your own personal gemstones in these workshop rings due to there being many variables and risks to your stone being damaged

Thank you for your understanding.

Workshop Details:

Dates: One-off session dates usually scheduled monthly.

Time: Saturdays, 1.00pm - 3.30pm

Location: Wellington Studio, situated on level 3, 22 Garrett St, Te Aro

Includes: All materials, tools, and delivery for a piece of jewellery cast in sterling silver weighing up to 12 gms)

Enquire about setting a gemstone, casting a ring heavier than 12 gms or casting in solid gold on the day.

name: Meet Japanese director Yukiko Sode
venue: Wallace Street, Mount Cook, Wellington 6021, New Zealand
long_description:
WELLINGTON - WIFT /NZIFF – SPECIAL EVENT - 15/8/26

Japanese film director Yukiko Sode is coming to the NZIFF with her film ALL THE LOVERS IN THE NIGHT.  (Cannes Un Certain Regard 2026)


As a preview to the film screening on Sunday 16th, we are holding a discussion with her in The Tea Gardens.

Date: Saturday 15th August

Time: 10.30 – 11.30 am

Location: The Tea Garden, Upper-floor function and event space, Dominion Museum Building (Block 10), Massey University's Pukeahu Wellington Campus

Free Entry!

Facilitated by Director Kathy McRae.


Yukiko Sode is an acclaimed Japanese director and screenwriter. She started out making independent, low-budget films, and her latest project, All the Lovers in the Night, is her fourth feature film. Its recent selection for the Cannes Film Festival marks an exciting new milestone in her career.

After getting married and becoming a mother, she moved from busy Tokyo to the beautiful coastal city of Kanazawa in Ishikawa Prefecture. There, she has intentionally built a lifestyle that beautifully balances family, everyday life and filmmaking. Her journey offers a wonderful perspective on creativity, motherhood, and finding a healthy, sustainable way to work in the film industry.

Sode’s story is a beautiful reminder that artists can absolutely continue to grow their creative voices while embracing the wonderful changes in their personal lives. 
Director Sode is a board member of action4cinema, a filmmaker coalition working to support independent cinema, protect art-house theatres, and create a more sustainable and fair environment for filmmakers in Japan.

 

This discussion previews the AWITO screenings at Massey; 12:15

If you’re coming along to those films, this is a great opportunity to squeeze in another event!

long_description:
Presenting our first ever Girls Torque in NZ. Be entertained by some of Te Whanganui-a-Tara's finest wāhine DJs.

M.Cap · Fortuna · Malware · Claire-voyant · Fluffcore

Girls Torque began in London in 2004 at the legendary Fridge in Brixton. A time when putting wāhine behind the decks was still a statement. Two decades on, the scene has transformed. The talent is undeniable, the ranks are deep, and the dancefloor belongs to everyone. We're bringing that spirit home to Aotearoa.

This lineup includes names woven into the fabric of the scene. Beyond the decks, you'll find them as DJ tutors, promoters, and event organisers, where they give back as much as they bring to the dancefloor.

• M.Cap is the founder of 'Nine Oh Nine' who facilitate girls & Femmes only DJ workshops.

• Fortuna is the founder of 'Fortunes' known for their deep/prog/melodic house & techno events.

• Malware is the Co-founder of Venom Events who focus on Techno events here in Pōneke.

• Claire-voyant is one of the founders of Torque Sounds and the original Girls Torque event back in London.

• Fluffcore is the Co-founder of TGF known for their dark techno events.

Join us at Valhalla on Saturday 15th August, 9pm to 3am, for a night of great music on on our Torque Sounds system, a Tubs Audio build.

Our kaupapa is simple: manaakitanga on the dancefloor. Girls Torque is open to all, celebrating all. Come and kanikani to your hearts content, respect and look out for each other.

id: IP Wānanga - Te Whanganui-a-Tara-3 Market Lane, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: IP Wānanga - Te Whanganui-a-Tara
venue: 3 Market Lane, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
Every story is rich in whakapapa and mātauranga. Join us for a powerful wānanga exploring how intellectual property can protect, strengthen, and preserve Indigenous storytelling across stage, screen, and beyond.

We welcome you to a wānanga that unpacks the foundations of intellectual property through both legal and tikanga Māori landscapes. We will explore the concept of story sovereignty and discover practical ways to protect your cultural expressions from their earliest beginnings through to contracts, collaborations, and future opportunities. In the growing world of artificial intelligence, we’ll also examine how intellectual property can be used not only as a legal tool, but as a pathway for creatives to maintain tino rangatiratanga over their taonga katoa. Facilitated by Māori creatives and lawyers Hariata Moriarty and Jorja Heta with guest speaker, leading expert on indigenous intellectual property rights and Tumuaki of Kāhui Legal, Lynell Tuffery Huria, this will be a dynamic session where law and art intersect.

Whether you're an artist, filmmaker, writer, performer or simply passionate about knowing more, this wānanga will inspire meaningful kōrero, build practical knowledge, and empower you to confidently protect the stories that shape who we are.

Please note, all attendees must be Ngā Aho Whakaari members (sign up, it's free!)

About Jorja Heta

Jorja Heta (Ngāpuhi, Te Rarawa, Te Aupōuri) is a lawyer, poet, screenwriter and human rights policy advisor/analyst driven by an ethos of social justice and truth. Her creative works explore Māori identity, spirituality and the lived realities of wāhine māori. She is the first in her whānau to attend University and holds a Bachelor of Laws and Arts from the University of Auckland (admitted to the High Court in 2025). Jorja has worked for Amnesty International Aotearoa, leading research submissions on Government Bills, briefing international diplomats and writing national reports on the justice system. She received the 2024/25 Prime Minister’s Scholarship, during which she provided commercial legal services in Thailand. In Aotearoa, Jorja has provided legal aid for Waitangi Tribunal claims and facilitated social justice wānanga at Parliament, centring the voices of those with lived experience of incarceration. She has undertaken research positions examining intellectual property in NZ and is interested in developing legal frameworks that preserve taonga katoa guided by tikanga. Passionate about Māori storytelling, Jorja has been published in Māori journals Pūhia and Awa Wāhine, and most recently co-wrote the short film Kikokiko, directed and written by Matariki Bennett and produced by Hariata Moriarty, which received the 2025 New Zealand Film Commission He Kauahi Catalyst Funding. She is the current Tuia recipient for Wellington City Council, a mentoring programme that supports young Māori in developing their leadership skills and contributing to their communities. She hopes to continue blending her creative expression and legal pūkenga to serve communities and empower mana motuhake of iwi, hapū and whānau.

About Hariata Moriarty

Hariata Moriarty (Ngāti Toa Rangatira, Ngāti Koata, Ngāti Kahungunu ki te Wairoa, Ngā Puhi) is an actor, writer and producer whose practice is grounded in the Theatre Marae framework of Te Rākau. Raised within this kaupapa, she grew up immersed in a model of theatre as both creative expression and community transformation. For seven years, her whānau opened their home to rangatahi from CYFS (now Oranga Tamariki), where she witnessed firsthand the healing power of storytelling and its capacity to strengthen identity, connection and social change and has since dedicated her practice to kaupapa Māori storytelling.

With nearly two decades of experience across stage and screen, Hariata has established herself as a versatile performer. She is the co-creator and performer of the acclaimed theatre work Waenga, developed alongside her brother Tamati Moriarty. On screen, she has appeared in Cousins, Red, White and Brass, Belief, Te Kohu and Untold Tales of Tuteremoana, spanning both independent and large-scale productions. She has recently appeared in the solo production Not in Our Neighbourhood at Circa Theatre produced by Taki Rua.

Hariata is also co-founder of Hurō Productions, a whānau-led company dedicated to championing Māori storytelling. Most recently, she produced and acted in Kikokiko, directed by Matariki Bennett and written by Bennett and Jorja Heta, with producer Jane Holland.

Alongside her artistic practice, Hariata holds a Bachelor of Laws and is completing a Master of Māori Laws and Philosophy through Te Wānanga o Raukawa. She is particularly passionate about intellectual property and the protection of Māori taonga through stage and screen, exploring how creative practice and legal frameworks can work together to uphold cultural integrity. Guided by Te Ao Wairua, she views storytelling as a vehicle for cultural preservation, knowledge sharing and social change, creating work that centres kaupapa Māori values and resonates with audiences both in Aotearoa and internationally.

id: VĀRUA: Imagining a Queer Pacific Screen-level 2/27 Dixon Street, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: VĀRUA: Imagining a Queer Pacific Screen
venue: level 2/27 Dixon Street, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
VĀRUA: Imagining a Queer Pacific screen is a programme featuring a screening of three moving image works by Sue Pearson and Pauline Reynolds, Latamai Katoa, and Samson Dell, followed by a conversation with artists Iz Randell, Latamai Katoa, and Samson Dell, moderated by Mauatua Fa’ara-Reynolds. Together, they will respond to the works and discuss the reparative capacity of moving image for queer Indigenous Pacific artists.

VĀRUA: Imagining a Queer Pacific screen is the concluding event forTHE UNDERWORLD, a pop-up installation by Latamai Katoa which relishes the sensuality of being seen whilst interrogating the very act of watching. Shown at CIRCUIT from 12-5pm 20-21 August, the installation is set in the artist’s backyard at night where they perform sensual gestures through shifting screens and frosted windows. Sitting somewhere between the tender, theatrical, and quietly confrontational, THE UNDERWORLD negotiates the descent from private ritual to public performance. Ultimately, Katoa’s work negotiates the visibility of their body, encouraging us to consider: should we be watching this?

VĀRUA: Imagining a Queer Pacific screen is curated by CIRCUIT’s Mana Moana Resident Mauatua Fa’ara-Reynolds.

The Mana Moana Residency is a 3 month placement at CIRCUIT supported by Creative New Zealand. The residency supports an emerging Pasifika writer/curator to develop a body of work that increases the visibility of Pasifika artists working in the moving image. CIRCUIT’s 2026 resident is Mauatua Fa’ara-Reynolds, a Mā’ohi-Norf’k writer and tapa-maker based in Te Whanganui-a-Tara. In 2025 they completed their MA in Creative Writing at the IIML, where they received the Letteri Family Prize for Creative Non-Fiction.

VĀRUA: Imagining a Queer Pacific screen is presented alongside Mauatua’s accompanying essay series on circuit.org.nz, A huri i tō mata i te pō which considers how Pacific artists are reclaiming the screen to heal from colonial legacies and forge their own legacies. Read the first essay here.

long_description:
Get ready for the infamous halfway point of "The Return". The critically acclaimed Part 8: "Gotta Light?".

Widely considered the most experimental, provocative piece of art in the history of television, this cinematic masterpiece takes us on a surreal journey right back to the origin of the root of all evil.

So come join us at the Twin Peaks Townhall (aka: Newtown community centre). Bring some damn good joe, or a damn fine helmet, buckle up and strap yourself in for a stunningly beautiful and also horrendously horrific audiovisual maelstrom "through the darkness of future past that every fan longs to see."

We'll be playing Parts 7 and 8 from the "Z to A" Blu-ray projected from a 4K player onto a 5.5m x 3.7m screen.

Written by Mark Frost, David Lynch and directed by David Lynch.

This is what we will be watching :

David Lynch "Weather Report" and song of the day.

"Previously on Twin Peaks"

long_description:
LOMU (2026) is an intimate, feature-length documentary that explores the life and legacy of Tongan-Kiwi rugby legend Jonah Lomu.

We're raising funds for Special Olympics Te Whanganui-a-Tara. Here's a bit about the movie:

LOMU is an intimate, feature-length documentary that explores the life and legacy of Tongan-Kiwi rugby legend Jonah Lomu. Directed by Vea Mafile'o and Gavin Fitzgerald, the film traces his journey from the streets of South Auckland to global sporting superstardom, while uncovering his deeply private personal and health struggles.

Utilising never-before-seen personal archives and intimate interviews with family and teammates, the film sheds light on his cultural identity and his gruelling, lifelong battles with a severe kidney illness. You can watch the official trailer here.

But wait- there's more: EVERY TICKET includes the chance to win a spot prize!

Please share this invitation widely with family, friends and colleagues.

name: INTIMATE EARTH | Film Adjacent Experimental Film Symposium
venue: Wallace Street, Mount Cook, Wellington 6021, New Zealand
long_description:
Film Adjacent presents Intimate Earth, a symposium dedicated to the aesthetic, cultural and political energies of experimental film in Aotearoa and beyond. Intimate Earth celebrates ways of seeing in distinction to dominant modes of audio-visual media in the twenty-first century. The symposium will assemble artists, curators and audiences around micro and macrocosmic imaginations of a world otherwise. 

This will be a two-day event, featuring six programmes, multiple roundtable discussions, and a filmmaking workshop. Each day will run 1pm to 10pm. Attendees can come and go as they please.

We will be unveiling speakers, programmes, and workshop-signups in the lead up to the symposium. You can stay up to date with us via Instagram or our website

id: Against the Tide: Aotearoa New Zealand in World Affairs, Volume V, 2006-2025-11 Turnbull Street, Thorndon, Wellington 6011, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: Against the Tide: Aotearoa New Zealand in World Affairs, Volume V, 2006-2025
venue: 11 Turnbull Street, Thorndon, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
About the event

The NZIIA warmly invites you to the Wellington book launch of Against the Tide: Aotearoa New Zealand in World Affairs Volume V 2006-2025. The event features presentations, discussion and Q&A from the book’s editors and several of the expert contributors, including

Mathew Doidge

Sir Peter Gluckman

Catherine Grant Makokera

Bethan Greener

Colin Keating

Serena Kelly

Hamish McDougall

Robert G. Patman


There will be an informal networking opportunity over drinks and snacks at the event. 

Discounted copies of the book are available to purchase at the event, and online here.

The fifth volume in a series going back to 1945, Against the Tide questions the narrative that we live in a uniquely troubled world, and sets the mid-2020s against the longer arc of New Zealand’s engagement in world affairs. Through thematic chapters spanning two decades, the contributors illuminate what is new and what is long running, and what choices New Zealand now has as it faces rapid geopolitical, economic, technological and climate shifts. This volume offers essential historical context and practical insights for policymakers, academics, students, and anyone interested in informed public debate.

This is a flagship research publication published by the New Zealand Institute of International Affairs—Whare Tāwāhi-a-mahi i Aotearoa in collaboration with Te Herenga Waka University Press.

Edited by Hamish McDougall, Serena Kelly and Mathew Doidge, contributors include Vanessa Bramwell, Robert Broughton, Shine Choi, Christian Dietrich, Sir Peter Gluckman, Catherine Grant Makokera, Bethan Greener, Rhieve Grey (Ngāti Tūwharetoa, Ngāti Porou, Ngāti Raukawa), Stephanie Honey, Colin Keating, Jason Paul Mika (Tūhoe, Ngāti Awa, Whakatōhea, Ngāti Kahungunu), Mia Mikic, Robert G. Patman, Hema Sridhar, Carrie Stoddart-Smith (Ngāpuhi, Ngāti Whātua) and Annie Te One (Te Ātiawa, Ngāti Mutunga).

About the speakers

Mathew Doidge is a Senior Research Fellow at the University of Canterbury’s National Centre for Research on Europe. His research interests include European Union external relations, regionalism and inter-regionalism, development policy, and Europe-Asia relations. He has taught at universities in Germany, the United Kingdom and New Zealand. He is Editor of New Zealand International Review, on the Executive Committee of the European Studies Association of Australia and New Zealand (ESAANZ) and Editor-in-Chief of the Australian and New Zealand Journal of European Studies.

Sir Peter Gluckman is President of the International Science Council, Director of Koi Tū: Centre for Informed Futures and a Distinguished University Professor Emeritus of the University of Auckland. He was Chief Science Advisor to the Prime Minister of New Zealand (2009–2018) and science envoy for the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade (2012–2018). Amongst international awards he received the American Association for Advancement of Sciences Science Diplomacy award in 2016.

Catherine Grant Makokera is Executive Director of the New Zealand Institute of International Affairs. She is an experienced trade negotiator and trade policy expert, having worked in the public, private, and academic sectors. She has represented New Zealand at the World Trade Organization and the United Nations. She is also a Research Associate of the Public Policy Institute at the University of Auckland.

Bethan Greener is Head of the School of People, Environment and Planning and Professor of International Relations at Massey University. Her research focuses on how states and others seek to provide security and what this means for world order, and New Zealand foreign and defence policy. This has resulted in books on international policing (2009), police and military roles in peace and stability operations (2014, co-authored with Will Fish) and an edited collection on the New Zealand Army (2017).

Colin Keating is a former diplomat and international lawyer. He was New Zealand Ambassador to the UN and the Security Council. He founded the organisation ‘Security Council Report’ in New York and is a leading authority on the Council. He was Special Envoy for the Prime Minister and Advisor to the Government of New Zealand’s 2015-2016 UN Security Council term.

Serena Kelly is a senior lecturer above bar in Political Science and International Relations at the University of Canterbury. Her research includes international political communication, European Union diplomacy, and relations, presence and impact in, and with, the Asia-Pacific. Serena is national Chair of the New Zealand Institute of International Affairs, was Chair of the NZIIA Christchurch branch from 2017 to 2021 and is also Vice -President of the European Studies Association of Australia and New Zealand.

Hamish McDougall was Executive Director of the New Zealand Institute of International Affairs during the creation of this book. He is an international historian of the Cold War, decolonisation and New Zealand’s foreign and trade policies. He has authored a book, articles, and an award-winning Doctorate from the London School of Economics and Political Science (LSE) on New Zealand’s external relations in the 20th century. In 2026 he was awarded a Fulbright Scholarship to the Walsh School of Foreign Service, Georgetown University in Washington DC, where he is researching an international history of Nuclear-Free New Zealand. He is also a Research Associate at the Public Policy Institute, University of Auckland.

Robert G Patman is a professor of International Relations and an Inaugural Sesquicentennial Distinguished Chair (2019) at the University of Otago. He is former Head of the Department of Politics. He is also the author or editor of 14 scholarly books. He is a Fulbright Senior Scholar and Honorary Professor to the New Zealand Defence Force Command and Staff College, Trentham, and provides regular contributions to the national and international media on global issues and events.

id: No Offence Taken Tour with Andrew Doyle Wellington-Ground Floor/1 Molesworth Street, Pipitea, Wellington 6011, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: No Offence Taken Tour with Andrew Doyle Wellington
venue: Ground Floor/1 Molesworth Street, Pipitea, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
The Free Speech Union New Zealand is proud to present the No Offence Taken Tour with Andrew Doyle!

Comedy has always pushed against the edges of what's acceptable to say, and few people understand that better than Andrew Doyle. As the writer and comedian behind the satirical Twitter phenomenon Titania McGrath, Doyle has spent years skewering the absurdities of cancel culture, performative outrage, and a comedy scene increasingly nervous about its own punchlines. Join us for an evening exploring what happens when humour collides with a culture of offence and why the ability to speak freely matters far more than we give it credit for.

Expect frank conversation, sharp wit, and a few laughs because if we can't joke about it, can we really talk about it at all?

Join the Free Speech Union and Andrew Doyle for an unforgettable evening. Buy your tickets now!

📍Grand Hall, Ground Floor/1 Molesworth Street, Pipitea, Wellington 6011

📅 Tuesday 15th September

🕐 6:30pm-8:00pm 

🎙️ Guest Speaker: Andrew Doyle

Comedy has always pushed against the edges of what's acceptable to say, and few people understand that better than Andrew Doyle. As the writer and comedian behind the satirical Twitter phenomenon Titania McGrath, Doyle has spent years skewering the absurdities of cancel culture, performative outrage, and a comedy scene increasingly nervous about its own punchlines. Join us for an evening exploring what happens when humour collides with a culture of offence and why the ability to speak freely matters far more than we give it credit for.

Expect frank conversation, sharp wit, and a few laughs because if we can't joke about it, can we really talk about it at all?

Join the Free Speech Union and Andrew Doyle for an unforgettable evening. Buy your tickets now!

📍Grand Hall, Ground Floor/1 Molesworth Street, Pipitea, Wellington 6011

📅 Tuesday 15th September

🕐 6:30pm-8:00pm 

🎙️ Guest Speaker: Andrew Doyle

Join WWF-New Zealand for a pre-election debate bringing together representatives from New Zealand's political parties to discuss the future of our marine environment. Hear directly from party representatives as they outline their policies and priorities for protecting our ocean, restoring marine biodiversity, and ensuring healthy, resilient seas for future generations.

venue: 75 Featherston Street, Pipitea, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
Internationally we see major changes in power dynamics, disruption of trade, and greater uncertainty.  We need to understand how New Zealand will navigate this challenging environment. 

The event is set to be a lively discussion, moderated by Newsroom Sam Sachdeva, with Hon Todd McClay (National), MP's Vanushi Walters (labour) and Teanau Tuiono (Green), and Daniel Eb (TOP) sharing what they see as Aotearoa New Zealand’s role on the global stage, and their perspectives around international cooperation, development, and trade.

It will also explore Aotearoa New Zealand’s position in the Asia-Pacific region and how it can strengthen ties with Pacific Island nations and cultivate deeper partnerships.

The event runs from 5:30-7:30PM at the Rydges Hotel in Wellington.  

It is open to the public (registrations required), and attendees will have the opportunity to ask questions of the panellists during the Q&A session.

name: Mental Health & Addiction 2026 Election Debate
venue: 15 Dufferin Street, Mount Victoria, Wellington 6011, New Zealand  ·  Accessibility info
long_description:
Ahead of the 2026 General Election, come and engage with representatives from all leading political parties on their actions and priorities for mental health and addiction. 

Make your voice count:

Hear about political parties' stances, policies, and actions for mental health and addiction in Aotearoa New Zealand in what will be the 55th New Zealand government parliamentary terms and future terms.

Influence and shape political party positions on mental health, addiction and wellbeing and future government based on your own knowledge and experiences.

Engage on wider issues including social determinants of health occurring within the health and social sector.

Get your tickets now to join us in Wellington, or if you are living outside of Wellington, join us via livestream.


We aim to make this event as accessible as possible. We will have NZSL interpreters for the event (both in person and live-streamed). Please get in touch with Louise at louise@platform.org.nz if you have any accessibility needs. 

Who is Platform?

Platform is a peak body and membership organisation representing the mental health and addiction non-governmental organisation (NGO) and community sector. We directly support 108 mental health and addiction NGOs and community organisations that provide support to tāngata whai ora (people seeking wellness) and whānau, including kaupapa Māori and Pasifika providers, and whānau and peer-led services. We also advocate for the wider network of mental health and addiction NGOs who share the same aspiration of a system and sector that is driven by the need for better and more equitable outcomes for all.

id: Unfiltered-11 Hutchison Road, Newtown, Wellington 6021, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: Unfiltered
venue: 11 Hutchison Road, Newtown, Wellington 6021, New Zealand
long_description:
Unfiltered
6pm - 8:30pm Saturday, 15th August.

Creative rest for Pōneke’s makers.

A night to come together and build a fortress from fabrics, sheets and circus silks. Creating a space that invites making for joy of it, without aiming for perfection. Once the fort is created, the floor will be opened up for people to share stories, quotes and poems, accompanied by snacks and hot drinks. The night will be topped off with an original story read aloud and a mini aerial hoop performance.

At the door you will be asked to sign a contract agreeing to leave your social and self expectation outside, for the night. So that thoughts like ‘I should talk more’ or ‘I talked too long’ or ‘that was a weird noise I made’ can be taken less seriously.

To prepare, choose a poem, quote or story, you might like to share. There will be no pressure on the night to participate in this. We invite you to notice the small details in the environments around you, leading up to the event.

We have a ‘no talking about work rule’. This is for the purpose of people relating to each other based on their interests, practices or passions, rather than how they make their living.

Come wearing warm comfy clothes. We will request that you turn your phone off during the workshop. This event is a fundraiser for The Circus Hub. Sliding scale pricing will available at the door.

$30 general entry

$15 students and community service card holders

$5-10 upon request. No questions asked.

id: Trades and Trailer 101-11 Hopper Street, Mount Cook, Wellington 6011, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: Trades and Trailer 101
venue: 11 Hopper Street, Mount Cook, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
Come join us for an open day at Cahoots for:


1) Workshop inductions - learn what amazing and gnarly things you can do at the Cahoots workshop! They have all sorts of tools from sanders and metal lathes to laser cutters and 3D printers. Closed toe shoes are a must. Please allow for 30min for the induction. The Cahoots crew will take you on an initial walk through the workshop along with a safety briefing. Tool training and full induction to obtain membership will be dependent on how quiet the workshop is on the day - so you may need to go back on another day to do this.

2) Our resident barber, Rhubarber, also doubles as a mechanic! They will take you through car engine maintenance, tyre changes, and show you how to kickstart a car.

3) Trailers! Learn how to properly hook and load a trailer.
If you have your NZ restricted/full car license, you have the chance to learn how to drive and back a trailer with an experienced person as your passenger princess. $5 fee applies to cover fuel (paid on the day). The car and trailer will be provided. Please allow for 20-30 mins, and expect to drive around the Mt Cook suburb. If you need an emotional support/hype crew, they can hop on the backseat while we drive around as long as they can be not distracting.

Additional notes:

It will be a drop in session kind of day but we would appreciate it if you could RSVP so we can make sure we have enough volunteers for the day!

You can give koha either through the Cahoots website or at the event on the day (via online bank or cash).

This is open for non-butches as well, as long as you please respect the community and kaupapa.

No SWERFs, No TERFs.

id: Book Club: Emiko by Chieri Uegaki-Level 2/57 Willis Street, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand  ·  Accessibility info-Humanitix
name: Book Club: Emiko by Chieri Uegaki
venue: Level 2/57 Willis Street, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand  ·  Accessibility info
long_description:
Join us in person to discuss Emiko, a contemporary version of Jane Austen's Emma set in Canada.

(Order your copy through us by 20 March 2026 for delivery at the 23 May meeting or couriered in NZ)

About Emiko:

A busybody foodie avoids questions of her own future as she meddles in the love lives of those around her. Has this matcha-maker met her match?

Self-declared matchmaking GENIUS (a la Beyonce) Emiko Kimori has already found success by helping her aunt find true love, so when the new girl in town becomes her new BFF, it's only natural for Emiko to help set her up for social success with a suitable love match.

Emiko lives with her Ojiichan in a small town on BC's West Coast surrounded by friends and neighbors, including her childhood friend Kenzo Sanada, who wishes she'd spend less time playing matchmaker. But Emiko can so clearly see who belongs together, even when her targets don't know it themselves. She simply has to meddle - for the sake of true love!

As for her own romantic life though . . . who has time for that? Emiko is far too busy with her matchmaking schemes, her brunch recipes, volunteering, her bustling social life, keeping up her grades, eating said brunch recipes and making plans for after graduation. Plans she will absolutely decide on soon. Definitely. Maybe? But when Emiko ends up falling for the last person she expects, she finds herself caught in the tangled web of her own love matches. For the first time, instead of arranging from afar, Emiko has to figure out what it means to be in love herself, and that friendship and romance are more complicated than she ever imagined . . .

About the Author:

Chieri Uegaki is a second generation Japanese-Canadian and award-winning children’s author living and writing on Vancouver Island, in the traditional and unceded territory of the lək̓ʷəŋən speaking peoples, today known as the Esquimalt and Songhees Nations.

She graduated with a Bachelor of Fine Arts from the University of British Columbia’s Creative Writing Department and has written a number of stories for children, including the picture books Suki’s Kimono and Rosie and Buttercup (both illustrated by Stéphane Jorisch); Hana Hashimoto, Sixth Violin (illustrated by Qin Leng); and Ojiichan’s Gift (illustrated by Genevieve Simms).

When not reading or writing, Chieri consumes rom-coms and mysteries in any form, chooses appetizers over dessert most of the time, and tries to stay on top of her collecting problem. She is currently working on a number of projects.

Rachel Pilois (Book Buyer) on this selection:

There have been many retellings of Austen’s novels in the last 200 years. Pride and Prejudice easily wins the prize of Austen’s most adapted novel in both film and literature. In the last 20 years there’s been a noticeable growth in culturally (and gender) diverse takes on Austen’s work, with the most popular retellings being of Indian (i.e Bride and Prejudice) or African-American (i.e. Ibi Zoboi’s Pride) heritage. Sadly, some of her less popular novels (Mansfield Park and Northanger Abbey) have few adaptations in both film and literature, faithful or modern retelling.

With the 2026 theme of the JASNZ being diversity it made sense to choose a slightly less popular novel (only in terms of how many adaptations) and a slightly less common culture used in Austen retellings. Thus I settled on the upcoming YA novel Emiko by Chieri Uegaki, a Japanese-Canadian retelling of Emma.

Emma is a much beloved story and a much beloved character, who’s thoughts, actions and motivations are very recognisable in a modern teenager. Adding in the deep cultural etiquette of Japan as a likeness to the rules of regency society, makes Uegaki’s Emiko a brilliant and well thought out modern retelling of the Emma.

As it publishes on 9 September 2025, we can discover and discuss this new and exciting adaptation for the first time together! 

NB: Ticket numbers are limited to ensure ease of discussion. Afternoon tea is provided

FRIEND: bring a friend, get 10% off! Discount automatically applied

We aim to provide an accessible and safe environment. Discounts are available for nonwaged members, early birds, volunteers and people buying multiple tickets. Please let us know how we can ensure you're included.

name: Dungeons & Flagons - An August Action
venue: 31 Whitehouse Road, Tītahi Bay, Porirua 5022, New Zealand
long_description:
Every great Dungeons and Dragons adventure begins in a tavern.

Whether you’re a seasoned adventurer or you’ve never rolled a die in your life, this two-hour, beginner-friendly D&D experience at Titahi Bay’s own Beer Engine is for you.

Turn up solo or with friends and be guided through a fast-paced adventure by a professional Dungeon Master. Choose your hero — a silver-tongued bard, a fire-flinging wizard, a sword-swinging fighter, a sneaky rogue, or something else entirely, with all characters, dice, and rules provided.

Expect laughs, ridiculous moments, and just enough danger to make the beer taste sweeter. Because while you’re swinging swords and slinging spells, the bar will be open with Beer Engine’s excellent selection of craft brews on tap.

No prep. No pressure. Just great beer and a story you’ll still be talking about afterwards.

The inaugural Dungeons and Flagons sold out in a week - so book fast, adventurer!

This is an age 18+ event.

About the Author: Chieri Uegaki is a second generation Japanese-Canadian and award-winning children’s author living and writing on Vancouver Island, in the traditional and unceded territory of the lək̓ʷəŋən speaking peoples, today known as the Esquimalt and Songhees Nations.
Adding in the deep cultural etiquette of Japan as a likeness to the rules of regency society, makes Uegaki’s Emiko a brilliant and well thought out modern retelling of the Emma.

id: Clay and Sip blue tile workshop-39 Abel Smith Street, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: Clay and Sip blue tile workshop
venue: 39 Abel Smith Street, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
A fabulous and fun workshop that combines creativity and clay whilst sipping a beverage of your choice for a relaxing and unique experience.

Create a stunning tile and decorate with impressed flower, heart, and leaf sprigs, fabrics and more. Around 4 weeks after the class these will be fired and glazed using a brilliant turquoise blue earthenware glaze, creating a gorgeous art piece to hang in your home or gift to another.

Alongside that sip a delicious drink from the Southern Cross Bar where we will be working.

Working with clay is good for the soul! Immersing in a gentle creative activity helps to switch off a busy mind, and making these is fun, relaxing and achievable even if this is your first time using clay.

All materials are provided so all you need to do is turn up ready to have some fun and creativity. Ticket includes all materials, double kiln firing, glaze and a drink valued up to $10. Tickets are non-refundable but fully transferable to a friend.

Venue information: seating capacity is for 12 people. There is no seating plan so if you're booking as a large group you may like to arrive early to ensure sitting together.

Completed pieces are ready to collect from the Southern Cross around 4 weeks after the class. 

Absolute care and expertise is taken with firing and glazing each piece but please note that the nature of clay and kiln firing can be unpredictable, carries a risk and glaze variations can happen (which is part of the excitement too!).

Like Wickham and Darcy, deep seated rivalry and dislike often shapes the events and emotions of Austen's work. Whether it is two suitors competing for the same quarry, or two families fighting over inheritance, this session will explore characters who seek both reconciliation and revenge.

id: Unfiltered-11 Hutchison Road, Newtown, Wellington 6021, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: Unfiltered
venue: 11 Hutchison Road, Newtown, Wellington 6021, New Zealand
long_description:
Unfiltered
6pm - 8:30pm Saturday, 15th August.

Creative rest for Pōneke’s makers.

A night to come together and build a fortress from fabrics, sheets and circus silks. Creating a space that invites making for joy of it, without aiming for perfection. Once the fort is created, the floor will be opened up for people to share stories, quotes and poems, accompanied by snacks and hot drinks. The night will be topped off with an original story read aloud and a mini aerial hoop performance.

At the door you will be asked to sign a contract agreeing to leave your social and self expectation outside, for the night. So that thoughts like ‘I should talk more’ or ‘I talked too long’ or ‘that was a weird noise I made’ can be taken less seriously.

To prepare, choose a poem, quote or story, you might like to share. There will be no pressure on the night to participate in this. We invite you to notice the small details in the environments around you, leading up to the event.

We have a ‘no talking about work rule’. This is for the purpose of people relating to each other based on their interests, practices or passions, rather than how they make their living.

Come wearing warm comfy clothes. We will request that you turn your phone off during the workshop. This event is a fundraiser for The Circus Hub. Sliding scale pricing will available at the door.

$30 general entry

$15 students and community service card holders

$5-10 upon request. No questions asked.

id: Trades and Trailer 101-11 Hopper Street, Mount Cook, Wellington 6011, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: Trades and Trailer 101
venue: 11 Hopper Street, Mount Cook, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
Come join us for an open day at Cahoots for:


1) Workshop inductions - learn what amazing and gnarly things you can do at the Cahoots workshop! They have all sorts of tools from sanders and metal lathes to laser cutters and 3D printers. Closed toe shoes are a must. Please allow for 30min for the induction. The Cahoots crew will take you on an initial walk through the workshop along with a safety briefing. Tool training and full induction to obtain membership will be dependent on how quiet the workshop is on the day - so you may need to go back on another day to do this.

2) Our resident barber, Rhubarber, also doubles as a mechanic! They will take you through car engine maintenance, tyre changes, and show you how to kickstart a car.

3) Trailers! Learn how to properly hook and load a trailer.
If you have your NZ restricted/full car license, you have the chance to learn how to drive and back a trailer with an experienced person as your passenger princess. $5 fee applies to cover fuel (paid on the day). The car and trailer will be provided. Please allow for 20-30 mins, and expect to drive around the Mt Cook suburb. If you need an emotional support/hype crew, they can hop on the backseat while we drive around as long as they can be not distracting.

Additional notes:

It will be a drop in session kind of day but we would appreciate it if you could RSVP so we can make sure we have enough volunteers for the day!

You can give koha either through the Cahoots website or at the event on the day (via online bank or cash).

This is open for non-butches as well, as long as you please respect the community and kaupapa.

No SWERFs, No TERFs.

id: Power Up Wainuiomata-1A Queen Street, Wainuiomata, Lower Hutt 5014, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: Power Up Wainuiomata
venue: 1A Queen Street, Wainuiomata, Lower Hutt 5014, New Zealand
long_description:
Power Up the Hutt – Wainuiomata

What if your home could be warmer, healthier, more comfortable – and cost less to run?

Across the Hutt Valley, more and more households are discovering that small changes to the way they power their homes can make a real difference. Lower energy bills, greater comfort through every season, cleaner air indoors, and more control over household costs are all within reach.

Join us at the Wainuiomata Neighbourhood Hub on Wednesday 16 September at 7:30 pm for a free community evening exploring how everyday families are making their homes work better for them.

Hosted by local volunteers who have already been on the electrification journey, this relaxed and informative session is all about sharing real experiences. You'll hear from people who have made changes such as installing heat pumps, solar panels, home batteries, electric hot water systems, induction cooktops, and electric vehicles. They'll talk honestly about the costs, the savings, the lessons they learned, and the improvements they've enjoyed in their daily lives.

Whether you're looking to reduce your household expenses, create a healthier home for your family, prepare for rising energy costs, or simply understand what your options are, this evening will help you take the next step with confidence.

There are no sales pitches and no technical knowledge required—just practical advice, friendly conversation, and the opportunity to ask questions in a welcoming environment.

Businesses, schools and community organisations interested in electrification are also welcome.

Free admission. Everyone welcome.

Come along and discover how making the switch can help you enjoy a more comfortable, affordable and resilient home for years to come.

long_description:
Are rising energy bills eating into your budget? Is your home as prepared as it could be for whatever the weather throws at it?

Electrify the Capital is a free expo designed to help everyday households take practical steps toward lower power bills and a more resilient home — without needing to be a tech expert or have a big budget to get started.

Come along and talk directly with local experts and providers who can show you what's actually possible for homes like yours. Whether you're renting or you own, whether you're just starting to explore your options or you're ready to make a move, there's something here for you.

At the expo you'll be able to:

Find out how much you could realistically save on your power bills each year

Understand what changes make the most difference for homes in this region

Learn how to keep your household running during power outages and extreme weather

Get straightforward advice tailored to your situation — not a sales pitch

Compare options and costs side by side, all in one place

This is about making your home work harder for you — spending less on energy, and feeling more confident that your household can handle whatever comes its way.

Entry is free. No prior knowledge needed. Just bring your questions.

There will be a family zone with activities for kids, and light refreshments available on site.

Come along to the TSB Arena on Saturday 17th October between 9am and 4pm!

Power Up the Hutt – Central Lower Hutt

A more comfortable home. Lower energy bills. Greater peace of mind.

If you've been wondering whether electrification could make a real difference to your home and your household budget, this free community event is the perfect place to start.

Join us at Hutt Bowling Club, 6 bMyrtle Street on Thursday 29 October at 7:30 pm for an informative and welcoming evening where local people share how they've transformed the way they live.

From warmer homes in winter and lower running costs to cleaner indoor air and greater energy independence, electrification is helping Hutt Valley households enjoy a better quality of life while reducing their environmental impact.

You'll hear firsthand experiences from local residents who have installed heat pumps, solar panels, home batteries, electric hot water systems, induction cooktops and electric vehicles. They'll explain what motivated them, what the process was like, what they would do differently, and the benefits they're now enjoying every day.

Whether you're just beginning to explore your options or you're ready to take the next step, you'll leave with practical ideas, greater confidence, and a clearer understanding of where to begin.

This is a community event—not a sales presentation. There are no technical lectures or pressure to buy anything. Just honest conversations, practical advice, and the opportunity to ask questions in a relaxed and friendly setting.

Businesses, schools and community organisations interested in electrification are also welcome.

Free admission. Everyone welcome.

Come along and discover how simple changes today can create a home that's more comfortable, more affordable to run, and better prepared for the future.

id: Software Freedom Day Wellington 2026-Murphy Building 21d Kelburn Parade, Kelburn, Wellington 6012, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: Software Freedom Day Wellington 2026
venue: Murphy Building 21d Kelburn Parade, Kelburn, Wellington 6012, New Zealand
long_description:
Software Freedom Day Wellington 2026

Software Freedom Day is a worldwide celebration of Free and Open Source Software.

This year we are bringing it back to Wellington!

Venue

Thanks to the Victoria Engineering Club, we have a room at Victoria University of Wellington Te Herenga Waka:

Building: Murphy (MY)

Room: MY501

Capacity: 50 people

Time: 10:00–16:00

The Murphy Building is on the Kelburn campus, easily accessible by cable car or bus.

Programme

Cathedral in the morning, Bazaar in the afternoon

The day will follow a "Cathedral and Bazaar" format: starting with talks from invited speakers, then opening up into a more collaborative, community-driven afternoon.

Morning Talks

The morning will focus on stories, ideas, and experiences from the Free and Open Source Software community.

Opening Karakia — we are looking for someone to open the event with a karakia. If you can help, get in touch.

Michael Tiemann — A career in Open Source technology, and why you should too. Michael has been a pioneer in the Open Source world and has a story worth hearing.

Kristina Hoeppner — what it's like to manage an open source product. Kristina is the Project Lead for Mahara, the open source ePortfolio platform. She'll share the reality of shepherding a global open source project: community, roadmaps, funding, and keeping the lights on.

We are still looking for maybe one more presenter in the morning, If you have something to share about Free and Open Source Software, email john@opsdev.nz.

Afternoon Bazaar

In the afternoon, the event becomes a space for the community to organise itself. Bring a topic, a project, a question, a demonstration, or an idea to share.

We will have facilitators on hand who will lead some ice breaker activities and space for workshops, breakout discussions, group-hosted tables, and demonstrations. Participants will be able to form groups around topics that interest them, share knowledge, and explore ideas together. Groups may also have the opportunity to share a short summary of their discussions with everyone at the end of the day.

There will also be a GPG key signing session running in the afternoon.

The Bazaar is intentionally open-ended. The goal is to create a space where Free and Open Source Software enthusiasts, students, developers, users, and curious newcomers can connect, collaborate, and learn from each other.

Support The Event

Donations for Software Freedom Day Wellington 2026 are managed through the

OpsDev.nz OpenCollective project:

https://opencollective.com/opsdevnz/projects/software-freedom-day-wellington-2026

id: Climate Fresk Workshop in Wellington-2/57 Willis Street, Wellington Central, Wellington 6011, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: Climate Fresk Workshop in Wellington
venue: 2/57 Willis Street, Wellington Central, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
https://events.humanitix.com/climate-fresk-workshop-in-wellington

Do you want to be part of the solution to tackle climate change but don’t have the time to become a climate scientist? Join us for a 3-hour interactive workshop to explore the causes and consequences of climate disturbances.

Based on the IPCC report and played by over 2 million people worldwide, this collaborative workshop allows you to understand the key issues of climate change to empower you to take action.

How it works:

The workshop is based on a 42-card game. Each card represents an element, a cause or a consequence of climate change.

In teams, guided by your facilitator, you are encouraged to find the cause-effect relationship between the different components of climate change. Collective intelligence will get you from one deck of card to the next!

This step-by-step reconstruction provides keys to understand the complexity and develop an overview of climate change.

Agenda:

Introduction, 15 mins

Fresk Card Game, 1 1/2 hours

Debrief and Actions, 1 hour 15 mins

Climate Fresk is an excellent opportunity to understand the key elements of climate change and what you can do to be part of the solution. No previous climate knowledge is needed.

Pizza will be served during the short break. Workshop run by Climate Training Co. Ltd.

id: FLINT Wellington: How Not To Spiral - A Fireside Chat On How Resilience Is Actually Built-2/45 Johnston Street, Wellington Central, Wellington 6011, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: FLINT Wellington: How Not To Spiral - A Fireside Chat On How Resilience Is Actually Built
venue: 2/45 Johnston Street, Wellington Central, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
Welcome to our How Not To Spiral - A Fireside Chat On How Resilience Is Actually Built event in Wellington.

We know resilience matters. What we talk about far less is how it’s built.

The saying goes: if life gives you lemons, make lemonade.

But is resilience the lemonade – or the skill you use to make it?

Curious? We are too. 

Our speakers will answer questions like:

Can you deliberately build resilience?

If resilience were on a job description, what would you actually look for in an applicant’s cover letter, CV or interview?

Does resilience in one area transfer to another – and, if so, does it just happen?

How do you know when to keep going and when to change direction?

The aim is not for you to leave inspired only by other people’s resilience. It’s for you to leave inspired by your own capacity for it – with a clearer understanding of:

how resilience develops

what you can do to build more of it

how you can demonstrate that you have it

Register today! It's free for members.

id: Searching for Life Beyond Earth: Lessons from Antarctica-33 Bunny Street, Pipitea, Wellington 6011, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: Searching for Life Beyond Earth: Lessons from Antarctica
venue: 33 Bunny Street, Pipitea, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
For most of Earth’s history, life was microscopic and, even today, microorganisms dominate the planet. If life exists beyond Earth, scientists believe it likely began as microorganisms and may remain at this stage.

Although covered with ice, several moons of the outer Solar System contain subsurface oceans holding many times the volume of liquid water found on Earth. These oceans may provide the greatest volume of habitable space in our Solar System, with Jupiter’s moon Europa holding perhaps the greatest potential as a modern habitat for microbial life.

More than 600 Antarctic subglacial lakes—estimated collectively to contain about 7% of all lake water on Earth—provide examples of how life can adapt to cold, dark environments comparable to Europa.

In this special public presentation, Professor John Priscu will describe biologically functional subglacial ecosystems in Antarctica and consider them alongside what we know about the geochemistry of Europa. Together, the evidence provides a compelling case that Europa’s sub-ice ocean could support microbial life—and possibly a second origin of life, independent of Earth.

Discovering life on Europa or elsewhere in the outer Solar System would have an enormous impact on science and society.

The presentation will be followed by audience questions.

18:00 – Welcome and introduction 

18:10 – Professor Priscu’s presentation 

18:55 – Audience Q&A 

19:30 – Event concludes 

This event is presented collaboratively by the New Zealand Astrobiology Network and Te Herenga Waka—Victoria University of Wellington. Professor Priscu's visit to Aotearoa New Zealand is supported by the Embassy of the United States in New Zealand.

long_description:
If you’re new here, welcome - stoked you found us!

We’re tipsy trails. We’re on a mission to get more people in their 20s outdoors and turn an online community into a seriously epic in-person one.

We walk together along some of New Zealand’s most stunning trails, chatting with new and old mates - usually wrapping things up with a well-earned beverage afterwards.

We’re a club built on the idea that getting outdoors doesn’t have to be super serious or intense - it should be accessible, with a bit of fun. You don’t need fancy gear. You don’t need to be “outdoorsy.” You don’t even need a group to come with - rocking up solo is totally normal here. All paces and abilities are welcome. You just need to show up and enjoy the rest.

So, what do you say? Put down your phone and come outside with us.

⛰️ TRAIL INFO

Trail: Ataturk Memorial and Breaker Bay via Eastern Walkway, Miramar Peninsula, Wellington

Length: Out & back, approx. 7km, 233m elevation gain, around 2 - 2.5 hours

Difficulty: Rated Moderate by AllTrails

🎒 WHAT TO BRING?

Water bottle (make sure it’s full!)

comfy walking shoes,

a warm layer for during and after the hike 🧥,

a waterproof jacket (just in case 🌧️),

trail snacks (interpret this however your heart desires),

hat, sunglasses, and sunscreen (fingers crossed for sunshine ☀️),

a bag to throw everything in (backpack or side bag works perfectly 🎒)

📍 MEETING POINT

Meeting details and timing will be emailed once you’ve registered.

Keep an eye on our Instagram and tipsy trails Facebook messenger group chats for any updates or weather changes.

🍻 POST-HIKE PLANS?

With the trail wrapped up and the afternoon still ahead, we’ll head to a nearby pub for a well-earned beverage and bite to eat!


🚙 NEED / CAN OFFER A LIFT

Carpooling is available for anyone who needs a lift or can offer one. Once you have registered, you can connect with others in the Facebook messenger carpool group chat, share your area, and organise pick-up details directly.

🥾 REGISTRATION

This is a free community event with limited spots. Registration is required.

Got questions? Our DM’s are always open on Instagram @tipsy_____________
